topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Drawing from Observation
topics.description: Looking closely at a real thing, such as a leaf, a shoe or a pet, and drawing what is actually there rather than what we expect: its outline, parts and details.
evidence: Draws a real object while looking at it, not from memory
Includes details they noticed, such as veins on a leaf
Compares the drawing with the object and adds what is missing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw a leaf or a toy while looking at it and include details they can actually see?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Line and Shape in Pictures
topics.description: Lines can be thick or thin, straight, wavy or zigzag, and they make shapes and outlines; a filled dark shape becomes a silhouette.
evidence: Draws different kinds of lines on purpose
Builds a picture of an animal or house from simple shapes
Recognises a silhouette as a filled shape
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw straight, wavy and zigzag lines on purpose and build a picture from simple shapes?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Primary and Secondary Colours
topics.description: Red, yellow and blue are primary colours; mixing two of them makes orange, green or purple, and adding white or black makes a colour lighter or darker.
evidence: Names the three primary colours
Mixes paints to make orange, green and purple
Makes a colour lighter with white and darker with black
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} mix paints to make green, orange and purple from the primary colours?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Warm and Cool Colours
topics.description: Colours have moods: reds and oranges feel warm, blues and greens feel cool, and bright or muted colours change how a picture feels.
evidence: Sorts colours into warm and cool
Chooses colours to show a happy, calm or gloomy mood
Explains how the colours in a painting make them feel
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} choose warm or cool colours to make a picture feel cosy or cold, and explain why?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: The Colour Wheel and Colour Contrast
topics.description: The colour wheel arranges colours so that neighbours blend and opposites, such as red and green, make each other stand out; artists use contrasts of colour and of light and dark.
evidence: Places primary, secondary and in-between colours on a colour wheel
Names complementary pairs and shows how they make each other look brighter
Uses a light-dark or complementary contrast to make something stand out
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} use a colour wheel to find complementary colours and use them to make part of a picture stand out?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Painting with Watercolour and Gouache
topics.description: Different paints behave differently: gouache covers what is underneath, watercolour is transparent and can be layered, and brush strokes can be thick, thin, dabbed or smooth.
evidence: Uses a brush to make broad and fine strokes
Paints a transparent wash with watercolour
Explains the difference between opaque and transparent paint
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} paint a sky with a watercolour wash and add details on top with thicker paint?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Texture and Pattern
topics.description: Texture is how a surface feels or looks like it feels (rough, smooth, furry); pattern is a shape or mark repeated in a regular way.
evidence: Makes rubbings of different textures
Draws marks that show fur, bark or scales
Creates a repeating pattern on paper or fabric
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} show in a drawing whether something is furry, rough or smooth, and make a repeating pattern?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Composition: Arranging a Picture
topics.description: Artists plan where things go in a picture: what is big and important, what is in front or behind, how to balance the space and where the eye should look first.
evidence: Chooses portrait or landscape format to suit the subject
Places the main subject so it stands out
Explains how an artist led their eye around a painting
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} plan a picture so the most important thing stands out and the page feels balanced?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Showing Near and Far in a Picture
topics.description: Flat pictures can show depth: things further away are drawn smaller, higher up and paler, and nearer things overlap those behind them.
evidence: Draws distant objects smaller and higher on the page
Uses overlapping to show what is in front
Makes distant hills paler and less detailed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw a landscape where trees far away look smaller and paler than trees close by?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Linear Perspective
topics.description: Perspective drawing uses a horizon line and vanishing points so that parallel lines, like the sides of a road or a building, meet in the distance.
evidence: Draws a horizon line and a vanishing point
Draws a road or corridor in one-point perspective
Draws a box in two-point perspective
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw a road or hallway that seems to go into the distance using a vanishing point?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Light, Shadow and Shading
topics.description: Shading shows that an object is solid: the side facing the light is bright, the far side is dark, and the object casts a shadow; artists use hatching or blending to show this.
evidence: Identifies the light source, highlight and shadow on an object
Shades a ball or box so it looks three-dimensional
Uses hatching or blending for tone
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} shade a drawing of a ball so it looks round, with a highlight and a shadow?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Drawing People: Proportions and Movement
topics.description: People can be drawn more convincingly by knowing rough proportions of the body and face, and by showing poses such as walking, running or sitting.
evidence: Draws a figure with roughly correct body proportions
Shows a figure walking, running or sitting
Places eyes, nose and mouth in a face in sensible positions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw a person running or sitting so the body parts are in about the right proportions?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Portrait, Landscape and Still Life
topics.description: Artworks are grouped into genres by what they show: portraits show people, landscapes show places, still lifes show arranged objects, and there are also animal, everyday and history pictures.
evidence: Sorts paintings into portrait, landscape and still life
Sets up and draws a simple still life
Makes a self-portrait or a portrait of someone they know
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell whether a painting is a portrait, a landscape or a still life?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Illustrating a Story
topics.description: Pictures can tell or retell a story: choosing an important moment, showing the characters, the setting and the mood, as book illustrators do.
evidence: Draws a key moment from a fairy tale or their own story
Shows characters and where the story happens
Talks about how a book illustrator showed a character
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} choose an exciting moment from a story and draw it with the characters and setting?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Sketching and Developing Ideas
topics.description: Artists collect ideas and try things out before the final piece: quick sketches, notes and experiments in a sketchbook or portfolio, then choose and improve the best idea.
evidence: Keeps sketches and experiments in a sketchbook
Makes several quick versions before choosing one
Explains how the final work changed from the first idea
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make a few quick sketches of an idea and explain which one they chose and why?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Modelling with Clay
topics.description: Shaping clay or plasticine by pinching, rolling, pulling and joining to make animals, figures and simple pots that stand up and keep their form.
evidence: Models an animal from one piece by pulling and pinching
Rolls coils or slabs to make a small pot
Joins parts so they stay together
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} model an animal or a little pot from clay or plasticine that holds together?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Paper Sculpture and Construction
topics.description: Turning flat paper or card into 3-D forms by folding, curling, cutting slits and gluing, to build models such as a toy town or a pop-up.
evidence: Folds and glues paper into a box or cylinder
Curls, pleats and slots paper to make 3-D shapes
Builds a small model from card pieces
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make a standing 3-D model from paper by folding, cutting and gluing?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Collage and Mixed Media
topics.description: Making pictures by cutting, tearing and arranging papers, photos, fabric and found materials, sometimes combined with drawing or paint.
evidence: Cuts and tears paper to make a collage picture
Combines different materials in one artwork
Explains why they chose each material
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make a picture by cutting and arranging different papers and materials?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Printmaking
topics.description: A print is made by inking a surface and pressing it onto paper, so the same image can be repeated: stamps, stencils, monoprints, lino or relief prints.
evidence: Makes a repeated pattern with a stamp or stencil
Explains that a print comes out mirror-reversed
Makes a simple relief print from a carved or built-up block
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make a stamp or stencil and print the same picture several times?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Ornament and Decorative Patterns
topics.description: Ornament decorates objects with repeating motifs, often plant or geometric shapes, arranged in a strip, a circle or across a surface, usually using symmetry.
evidence: Designs a border pattern that repeats a motif
Uses symmetry to design a decoration
Finds plant and geometric motifs on decorated objects
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design a repeating border pattern using a symmetrical motif?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Folk Art and Traditional Crafts
topics.description: Every region has traditional crafts, such as embroidery, weaving, painted wood, pottery and toys, with typical motifs and colours handed down over generations.
evidence: Recognises some traditional crafts of their own country
Describes typical motifs and colours of a folk style
Tries a traditional technique such as weaving or embroidery
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name a traditional craft from their country and describe its typical patterns or colours?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Signs, Symbols and Pictograms
topics.description: Simple pictures can carry a message without words: road signs, pictograms, logos and map symbols work because they are simplified and easy to recognise.
evidence: Explains what common signs and pictograms mean
Designs a pictogram for a classroom rule
Simplifies a drawing so it can be recognised quickly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design a simple pictogram that others understand without words?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Posters: Combining Words and Pictures
topics.description: A poster, invitation or book cover joins image and lettering to catch attention and pass on a message clearly.
evidence: Plans a poster with a clear main image and title
Makes the most important words largest
Explains what makes a poster eye-catching
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design a poster where the picture and big title make the message clear at a glance?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Lettering and Typography
topics.description: Letters can be designed: their shape, size, weight and spacing change how a word looks and feels, from decorated initials to logos and clear headlines.
evidence: Draws decorative or block letters evenly
Chooses a lettering style that fits the message
Designs a simple word logo
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design lettering for a title so its style matches what it is about?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Designing Useful Objects
topics.description: Designers plan objects so that form follows function: thinking about who uses it, what it must do and which material suits, then sketching, testing and improving.
evidence: Describes what an everyday object must do and for whom
Sketches and labels a design for a useful object
Explains why a material or shape suits the purpose
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design a useful object, like a pencil case or a bag, and explain why its shape and material fit its use?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Buildings and Their Parts
topics.description: Buildings have parts such as walls, roofs, doors, windows, columns and towers, and their shape shows what they are for: homes, schools, churches, bridges.
evidence: Names the main parts of a building
Matches building types to what they are used for
Draws or builds a model of a building from observation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the main parts of a building and say what different buildings are used for?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Traditional Homes Around the World
topics.description: Traditional houses were built from local materials to suit the climate and way of life: log houses, adobe, stone houses, yurts and stilt houses.
evidence: Matches traditional houses to their materials
Explains how a house suits its climate
Describes the parts and decoration of a traditional house of their region
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why a yurt, a log house and a stone house are built so differently?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Plans, Views and Models
topics.description: Objects and rooms can be shown from above (plan), from the front and from the side, and built as scale models, as architects and designers do.
evidence: Draws a room or object seen from above
Matches front, side and top views of an object
Builds a simple model of a room or playground
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw a plan of their room as seen from above?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Architectural Styles Through History
topics.description: Buildings show their age: Greek temples with columns, Roman arches and domes, Romanesque round arches, Gothic pointed arches and tall windows, and modern steel and glass.
evidence: Recognises columns, round arches, pointed arches and domes
Matches famous buildings to their period
Explains how new materials changed buildings
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell a Greek temple, a Gothic cathedral and a modern skyscraper apart by their features?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Talking About Artworks
topics.description: Looking carefully at an artwork and saying what we see, how it makes us feel and why, using words such as colour, line, shape and mood, and listening to others’ views.
evidence: Describes what they see in a picture before giving an opinion
Says how an artwork makes them feel and why
Talks about their own and classmates’ artworks respectfully
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe a painting, say how it makes them feel and point to what causes that feeling?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Museums and Galleries
topics.description: Museums and galleries collect, protect and display art and objects; visitors can look, learn and respect the rules of the space.
evidence: Explains what museums and galleries are for
Finds and describes a favourite work during a visit
Follows museum rules
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a gallery is for and describe a work they liked on a visit?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Famous Artists and Their Works
topics.description: Getting to know some well-known artists, such as Leonardo da Vinci, Rembrandt, Van Gogh, Monet or Picasso, and artists from their own country, and recognising their typical style.
evidence: Names several artists and one work by each
Recognises an artist’s typical style
Makes a piece inspired by an artist’s way of working
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name a few famous artists and recognise a work by one of them?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Art Through the Ages
topics.description: Art changes over time: cave paintings, Egyptian and Greek art, medieval art, the Renaissance, Baroque, Impressionism and modern art each have typical subjects and ways of showing them.
evidence: Places major art periods in order
Describes typical features of the Renaissance and Impressionism
Explains how an artwork reflects its time
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} put cave art, the Renaissance, Impressionism and modern art in order and describe one of them?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Modern and Abstract Art
topics.description: Some artworks do not copy what we see: abstract art uses colour, line and shape for their own sake to express feelings or ideas, as Kandinsky, Klee or Miró did.
evidence: Explains the difference between figurative and abstract art
Describes the feeling of an abstract painting
Makes an abstract piece that expresses a mood
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what makes a painting abstract and make one that shows a feeling?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Taking Photographs: Framing and Viewpoint
topics.description: A photo depends on what is in the frame, how close you are and where you stand: close-ups, wide shots, high and low viewpoints and light change the result.
evidence: Frames a photo so the subject fills the picture
Takes the same subject from high, low and close viewpoints
Explains how light changes a photo
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} take a photo from an unusual viewpoint and explain how it changes the picture?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Comics and Storyboards
topics.description: A sequence of pictures can tell a story over time: comic panels, speech bubbles and storyboards plan what happens in each frame.
evidence: Draws a short comic strip with a beginning, middle and end
Uses speech bubbles and panel order correctly
Plans a short film scene as a storyboard
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell a short story in a comic strip of four or more panels?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: How Animation Works
topics.description: Animation shows many slightly different still pictures quickly one after another, so the eye sees movement: flip books, cartoons, stop motion and computer animation.
evidence: Explains why quick changing pictures look like movement
Makes a flip book or simple stop-motion clip
Names different kinds of animation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make a flip book or a short stop-motion animation and explain why it seems to move?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: How Images Persuade: Advertising
topics.description: Adverts and media use pictures, colours, sounds and words chosen to grab attention and make us want something; noticing these tricks helps tell real from made-up.
evidence: Points out what an advert wants the viewer to do
Identifies the colours, images and words used to persuade
Tells the difference between an advert and information
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how a TV or poster advert tries to make people want something?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Drawing with a Computer
topics.description: Using a simple graphics program to draw lines and shapes, fill colours, copy and repeat elements and make a picture or a pattern.
evidence: Uses pencil, shape, fill and eraser tools
Copies and repeats a shape to make a pattern
Saves and opens their picture
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make a picture in a drawing program using shape, fill and copy tools?

topics.subject: Visual Arts
topics.name: Art in Theatre: Sets and Costumes
topics.description: Artists design the look of plays, puppet shows and films: scenery, costumes, masks and puppets that show the time, place and characters.
evidence: Designs a costume that shows a character’s personality
Makes a simple set or puppet for a scene
Explains how scenery shows time and place
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design a costume or a stage set that shows who a character is and where the story happens?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: High and Low, Loud and Quiet Sounds
topics.description: Sounds differ in pitch (high or low), volume (loud or quiet), length (long or short) and tone colour, both in the world around us and in music.
evidence: Says whether a sound is higher or lower than another
Plays or sings loudly and quietly on purpose
Describes everyday and musical sounds by pitch, volume and length
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell which of two sounds is higher and play or sing something loudly and then quietly?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Keeping a Steady Beat
topics.description: Music has a steady pulse like a heartbeat; we can clap, march or tap along to it and keep it going together.
evidence: Claps or marches in time with music
Keeps a steady beat while others play a rhythm
Notices when the beat speeds up or slows down
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} clap or march in time to the beat of a song and keep it steady?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Rhythm: Long and Short Sounds
topics.description: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds and silences in music, such as the rhythm of words in a rhyme; patterns can be copied, repeated and invented.
evidence: Claps the rhythm of a rhyme or a name
Echoes a short rhythm clapped by someone else
Tells beat and rhythm apart
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} clap back a short rhythm and clap the rhythm of a familiar rhyme?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Tempo and Dynamics
topics.description: Tempo is how fast music goes and dynamics is how loud it is; musicians use Italian words such as allegro, andante, forte, piano and crescendo to describe them.
evidence: Describes music as fast or slow and loud or soft
Knows forte, piano, crescendo and allegro
Performs a song getting gradually louder or slower
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what forte and piano mean and sing a song getting gradually louder?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Metre: Strong and Weak Beats
topics.description: Beats are grouped in bars with a strong first beat: in twos or fours like a march, or in threes like a waltz; time signatures such as 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 show this.
evidence: Feels and claps the strong first beat of each bar
Tells a march in two from a waltz in three
Explains what 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 mean
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell whether a piece goes in twos like a march or in threes like a waltz?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Melody: Steps, Leaps and Shape
topics.description: A melody is a tune: notes moving up or down by steps or leaps, forming phrases with a shape that rises, falls or stays the same.
evidence: Shows with their hand whether a melody goes up or down
Tells steps from leaps
Sings back a short melodic phrase
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} show with their hand whether a tune moves up, down, by steps or by leaps?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Solfege and the Pentatonic Scale
topics.description: Notes can be sung with syllables do, re, mi, so, la (often with hand signs); the five-note pentatonic scale is used in children’s and folk songs in many cultures.
evidence: Sings so-mi and la-so-mi patterns with syllables or hand signs
Sings a pentatonic song in solfege
Notices that many folk songs use only five notes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} sing a simple tune using do-re-mi-so-la syllables or hand signs?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Major and Minor
topics.description: Scales and keys give music its colour: major often sounds bright and minor often sounds darker or sadder; a scale is a ladder of notes from the keynote.
evidence: Hears whether a piece is in major or minor
Sings or plays a major scale
Describes how major and minor sound different
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} hear whether a melody sounds major (bright) or minor (darker)?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Intervals
topics.description: An interval is the distance between two notes, from a semitone and a tone up to the octave; thirds, fifths and octaves sound smooth, seconds and sevenths sound tense.
evidence: Names intervals from a second to an octave
Counts the interval between two notes on the staff
Hears the difference between consonant and dissonant intervals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the interval between two notes, such as a third or a fifth?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Chords and Harmony
topics.description: Harmony is notes sounding together; a chord such as a major or minor triad is built from stacked thirds, and songs move through chord progressions that accompany the melody.
evidence: Builds a major and a minor triad
Plays a simple accompaniment with two or three chords
Follows chord symbols in a song
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} play a major and a minor chord and accompany a song with a few chords?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Timbre: Voices and Instrument Sounds
topics.description: Every voice and instrument has its own sound colour: children’s, women’s and men’s voices, and instruments that are blown, struck, shaken, plucked or bowed.
evidence: Recognises common instruments by their sound
Sorts instruments by how the sound is made
Tells children’s, women’s and men’s voices apart
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} recognise a few instruments by sound alone and say whether they are blown, struck or bowed?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Musical Form: Repetition and Contrast
topics.description: Music is built from parts that repeat or contrast: call and response, verse and chorus, AB, ABA and rondo (ABACA) forms.
evidence: Recognises when a section of music comes back
Labels a song’s sections as verse and chorus
Describes a piece as AB, ABA or rondo
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} notice when the first part of a piece comes back and describe it as ABA?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Theme and Variations
topics.description: A theme is a musical idea; composers vary it by changing its rhythm, speed, key, harmony or instruments while keeping it recognisable.
evidence: Recognises a theme when it returns changed
Describes how a variation differs from the theme
Makes a simple variation of a known tune
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} recognise a tune in a set of variations and say what has changed?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Syncopation and Dotted Rhythms
topics.description: Some rhythms play against the beat: dotted rhythms lengthen one note and shorten the next, and syncopation puts the accent off the beat, giving music swing and energy.
evidence: Claps a dotted rhythm accurately
Claps a syncopated rhythm against a steady beat
Hears syncopation in folk, pop or jazz music
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} clap a syncopated rhythm while someone else keeps a steady beat?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Compound Time: 6/8
topics.description: In compound time each beat divides into three, as in a jig or a lullaby; 6/8 has two beats per bar, each made of three quavers.
evidence: Feels two big beats in 6/8 music
Claps 6/8 rhythms with dotted notes
Tells 6/8 apart from 3/4
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} feel the swaying two-beat pulse of a piece in 6/8 and clap along?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Texture: Melody, Accompaniment and Polyphony
topics.description: Music can have one line (unison), a melody with accompaniment, or several independent melodies at once (polyphony), as in a round or a fugue.
evidence: Tells unison, melody with accompaniment and polyphony apart
Follows one voice in a two-part piece
Explains how a round creates polyphony
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell whether a piece has one tune with accompaniment or several tunes at once?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Drawing Sounds: Graphic Notation
topics.description: Sounds can be written as pictures: lines going up for rising pitch, big shapes for loud sounds, dots for short ones, so music can be read and played back.
evidence: Draws a sound picture of a short piece
Plays sounds from a simple graphic score
Matches a melody to a drawn melodic line
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw a picture of some sounds and then play them back from the drawing?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Reading and Writing Rhythms
topics.description: Note values show how long sounds last: whole, half, quarter and eighth notes and their rests; they are read in bars with bar lines and time signatures.
evidence: Names quarter notes, eighth-note pairs, half notes and rests
Claps a written rhythm
Writes down a short rhythm they hear
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} read and clap a short written rhythm with quarter notes, eighth notes and rests?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Reading Notes on the Staff
topics.description: The five-line staff shows pitch: notes sit on lines and in spaces, the treble clef fixes their names (C, D, E …), and higher notes are written higher.
evidence: Names notes on the treble staff
Finds written notes on a keyboard or glockenspiel
Writes a short melody on the staff
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name notes written on the treble staff and find them on an instrument?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Keys, Sharps, Flats and the Bass Clef
topics.description: Sharps and flats raise or lower notes, key signatures show which ones a piece uses, and the bass clef is used for low notes.
evidence: Explains what sharp, flat and natural signs do
Reads a key signature with one or two sharps or flats
Names notes in the bass clef
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a sharp or flat does and name a few notes in the bass clef?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Singing in Tune Together
topics.description: Singing with good posture and breathing, matching pitch, singing clearly and together as a group, and learning songs by ear and by heart.
evidence: Sings a learned song from memory in tune
Stands or sits well and breathes at phrase ends
Starts and stops together with the group
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} sing a familiar song in tune and together with others?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Singing Rounds and in Parts
topics.description: In a round (canon) groups sing the same tune starting at different times; later, singers hold their own part against another melody or harmony.
evidence: Holds their part in a two-part round
Sings an ostinato or harmony line against a melody
Listens to the other part while singing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} keep singing their own part in a round while others sing a different part?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Body Percussion and Rhythm Instruments
topics.description: Making rhythms with claps, pats, stamps and clicks and with drums, shakers and other untuned percussion, including repeated patterns (ostinato) to accompany songs.
evidence: Plays a rhythm with body percussion
Accompanies a song with a repeated rhythm on a percussion instrument
Plays together with others and keeps time
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} accompany a song with a repeating rhythm on a drum or with claps and stamps?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Playing a Melody Instrument
topics.description: Learning to play tunes on a melodic instrument such as recorder, glockenspiel, keyboard or ukulele, with correct technique and from memory or notation.
evidence: Plays a simple tune on a melodic instrument
Uses correct posture and fingering
Plays a part in a class ensemble
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} play a simple tune on an instrument such as recorder, glockenspiel or keyboard?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Moving and Dancing to Music
topics.description: Responding to music with movement: walking to the beat, showing high and low or fast and slow with the body, and learning simple folk, circle and children’s dances.
evidence: Moves in time to music
Shows changes in tempo or dynamics with movement
Performs a simple circle or folk dance
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} move in time to music and learn the steps of a simple circle dance?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Improvising Rhythms and Tunes
topics.description: Making up music on the spot: answering a rhythm or melody with your own, using voices, body percussion or instruments, and creating sound pictures for a story or poem.
evidence: Answers a clapped or sung question with their own phrase
Improvises using only a few given notes
Creates a soundscape for a story
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make up a short answer to a clapped or sung musical question?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Composing a Short Piece
topics.description: Composing means planning music: choosing notes, rhythm and form, writing it down in some notation and performing or recording it.
evidence: Composes a short melody of four bars
Writes their piece in graphic or standard notation
Performs and improves their composition
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} compose a short tune, write it down and play it to someone?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Making Music with Digital Tools
topics.description: Using apps and software to record, loop, layer and edit sounds, write notation or create beats and electronic music.
evidence: Records and loops sounds in an app
Layers several tracks into a short piece
Uses notation or sequencing software
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} create a short piece in a music app by recording, looping and layering sounds?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Listening to Music and Describing It
topics.description: Listening with attention to the whole piece and describing its mood, speed, loudness, instruments and what it reminds us of, in words, drawings or movement.
evidence: Listens quietly to a whole short piece
Describes the mood of the music with suitable words
Shows what they heard through a drawing or movement
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} listen to a short piece and describe how it sounds and how it makes them feel?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Instruments of the Orchestra
topics.description: The orchestra has four families, strings, woodwind, brass and percussion, led by a conductor; each family makes sound in its own way.
evidence: Names the four families of the orchestra
Recognises some orchestral instruments by sight and sound
Explains what a conductor does
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the four families of the orchestra and recognise a few instruments by sound?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Music That Tells a Story
topics.description: Programme music paints pictures or tells stories without words, like Peter and the Wolf, The Carnival of the Animals or The Four Seasons, using instruments and themes for characters.
evidence: Identifies which instrument plays which character
Describes the scene the music paints
Explains how the music shows what happens
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} say which character each instrument plays in Peter and the Wolf or a similar piece?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Opera and Ballet
topics.description: Opera tells a story through singing with orchestra (arias, choruses, overture); ballet tells it through dance and music; both are staged in theatres.
evidence: Explains the difference between opera and ballet
Names an aria, a chorus and an overture
Retells the story of an opera or ballet they watched
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how opera and ballet tell a story differently?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Musicals and Film Music
topics.description: Musicals combine songs, dialogue and dance; film music sets the mood, follows the action and gives characters their own themes.
evidence: Names a musical and describes how songs move the story on
Explains how film music changes the mood of a scene
Recognises a character theme in a film
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how the music in a film makes a scene feel exciting, sad or scary?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Folk Songs and Traditional Music
topics.description: Every people has folk songs, dances and instruments passed on by ear: lullabies, work songs, game songs and songs for festivals of the year.
evidence: Sings several folk or children’s songs of their own country
Names some traditional instruments
Explains when and why folk songs were sung
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} sing a few folk songs from their own country and say what they were sung for?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Music of World Cultures
topics.description: Music around the world sounds different: gamelan, African drumming, Latin American dances, Asian scales and instruments, and these traditions influence each other.
evidence: Recognises music from several world regions
Names an instrument typical of another culture
Describes how another tradition’s rhythm or scale sounds different
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} recognise music from a few world cultures and name one of their instruments?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Great Composers and Their Times
topics.description: Composers such as Bach, Mozart, Beethoven, Chopin or Tchaikovsky lived in particular places and times, which shaped their lives and the music they wrote.
evidence: Names several composers and one work by each
Tells a few facts from a composer’s life
Connects a composer to their time and place
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name a few great composers, one piece by each, and something about their lives?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Periods of Music History
topics.description: Western music has periods with typical sounds: medieval chant, Renaissance, Baroque, Classical, Romantic and 20th-century music.
evidence: Places the periods of music history in order
Describes typical features of Baroque, Classical and Romantic music
Matches composers to their period
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} put Baroque, Classical and Romantic music in order and say how they sound different?

topics.subject: Music
topics.name: Jazz, Blues and Popular Music
topics.description: Jazz and blues grew from African-American music with improvisation, swing and blue notes; they led to rock, pop and hip-hop, which use riffs, beats and verse-chorus songs.
evidence: Describes features of jazz such as improvisation and swing
Recognises the 12-bar blues
Names some popular music styles and their typical instruments
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe what makes jazz sound like jazz and name a few popular music styles?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Caring for Nature and Surroundings
topics.description: Taking responsibility for the natural and built surroundings: looking after a pet or a plant, tidying a shared space, noticing what makes a place orderly and pleasant, and suggesting small improvements
evidence: Describe one way they personally look after a plant, an animal or a shared place
Explain why a tidy, cared-for environment matters to people and living things
Suggest one practical improvement for their classroom, garden or street
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe how they help look after a plant, an animal or a shared place, and suggest one small way to make their surroundings better?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pollution and Endangered Species
topics.description: How pollution of air, water and soil harms living things and why some species are endangered; why protecting wildlife matters and how everyday choices such as waste and consumption affect it
evidence: Name main kinds of pollution and give an example of each
Explain how pollution or habitat loss can put a species in danger
Give examples of everyday habits that reduce waste and protect wildlife
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how pollution can harm animals and plants, and name a few everyday habits that help protect them?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Sustainable Living and Resource Ethics
topics.description: What sustainability means for personal habits and society: using natural resources, pollution and global inequality as ethical questions, and choosing actions that support a livable future
evidence: Explain what sustainable living means with examples from home and school
Describe an ethical question raised by using natural resources or by pollution
Choose and justify one habit they could change to support a sustainable future
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what sustainable living means and discuss one fairness question about how people use natural resources?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Shared Values in Traditional Stories
topics.description: Finding rules for living together in traditional and cultural stories: fairness, forgiveness, honesty, helping; telling right from wrong in examples and suggesting what a character could do differently
evidence: Retell a story and name the rule for living together it shows
Explain the difference between a right and a wrong action using an example
Suggest a better way for a character to act, or give a similar example from their own life
topics.assessmentPrompt: After hearing a traditional story, could {{name}} say what it teaches about treating others well and give an example from their own life?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Religious Festivals and Customs
topics.description: The main festivals of major religious traditions in Europe, such as Christmas, Easter, Pentecost, Hanukkah and Passover: the stories behind them, symbols, customs and how people celebrate
evidence: Name several religious festivals and the tradition each belongs to
Retell the story or event a festival remembers
Describe a symbol or custom connected with a festival
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name a few religious festivals, say what each one remembers, and describe a custom or symbol linked to it?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Moral Teachings of Major Religions
topics.description: What major world religions teach about how to live: love, respect for life, justice and forgiveness; how these teachings show up in daily life, culture and society, and the role religion plays in people's lives
evidence: Name moral teachings found in more than one religious tradition
Explain how such a teaching shows up in everyday life or in a cultural practice
Describe respectfully the role religion can play in a person's life and in a community
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe a moral teaching shared by several religions and explain, respectfully, how it appears in everyday life?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Roles and Bonds in the Family
topics.description: Roles and tasks of family members, what holds a family together (love, trust, respect), common family conflicts and difficult situations, ways to solve them and where to turn for help
evidence: Name the roles and tasks of different family members, including their own
Explain what love, trust and respect add to family and friendship relationships
Describe a family conflict or hard situation, suggest ways to deal with it and say where to find help
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe the roles in their family, suggest ways to handle a common family disagreement, and say whom to ask for help in a hard situation?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Deciding What to Share Online
topics.description: Choosing what personal information to share online and with whom: what counts as private, how shared content can spread, and rules for safe, respectful posting
evidence: List kinds of personal information that should stay private online
Explain how a post or photo can spread beyond the intended audience
Decide, with reasons, whether a given post is safe to share
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} look at a sample post or message and decide, with reasons, whether it is safe to share online?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: The Family as a Social Institution
topics.description: The family as a basic unit of society: how members cooperate and care for one another, how children learn values and habits in the family, and how generations stay connected
evidence: Explain what makes a family work: cooperation, mutual care, respect
Describe how children learn values and habits within the family
Compare how family life or roles have changed across generations
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why the family is considered a basic institution of society and how family roles have changed across generations?

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Family Finances and Saving
topics.description: How a household manages money: grouping income and expenses, planning a family budget, rational spending, forms of saving and financial tools households use, and making a simple personal financial plan
evidence: Sort a household's income and expenses into categories and compare them
Explain several ways of saving and what each is for
Draft a simple personal financial plan with a savings goal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} sort a household's income and spending into categories, compare ways of saving, and sketch a simple plan to reach a savings goal?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Our Town and Its Institutions
topics.description: Basic features of a town or village and the institutions and organisations that work there; how residents can propose and plan improvements to their locality together
evidence: Name institutions in their locality and say what each one does
Describe key features and history of their town or village
With others, write a simple proposal for improving the locality
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the main institutions in their town and, together with others, put forward a simple plan to improve something locally?

topics.subject: Geography
topics.name: Home Region and Its Landmarks
topics.description: Getting to know the home region: name of the town and region, notable places, cultural sites, well-known people and key events connected with the main city of the region
evidence: Give the name of their town or village and region
Name several notable places or cultural sites of the region
Tell about one well-known person or event connected with the region
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name their town and region and tell about a few notable places or people connected with it?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: National Symbols and the Capital City
topics.description: What a country's symbols are for (flag, emblem, anthem) and what a capital city is; recognising the symbols and the capital of their own country
evidence: Name the flag, emblem and anthem of their country and recognise them
Say what a capital city is and name their country's capital
Explain that symbols stand for a country or community
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} recognise their country's flag and name its capital city and explain what symbols like a flag are for?

topics.subject: Geography
topics.name: Countries and Peoples of the World
topics.description: That the world has many countries and peoples; the peoples living within one country; landmarks of nature and culture that are known as symbols of particular countries
evidence: Name several countries and peoples and show some on a map
Explain that many peoples can live in one country
Match a famous landmark with the country it is known for
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name several countries and peoples, and match some famous landmarks to the countries they belong to?

topics.subject: Geography
topics.name: Finding Your Country and Region on a Map
topics.description: Locating your own country, its capital and region on a globe, world map and administrative map; naming continents and oceans; neighbouring countries and regions
evidence: Find their country and capital on a world map or globe
Name the continents and oceans and point to them
Name neighbouring countries and show their own region or county on a map
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find their country, its capital and their own region on a map and name neighbouring countries?

topics.subject: Geography
topics.name: Compass Directions and Map Symbols
topics.description: Using a compass to find cardinal and intercardinal directions, reading common map symbols (landforms, water, settlements, roads, borders), telling map types apart and sketching a simple plan of a room or the school area
evidence: Use a compass to name the main and in-between directions
Read common map symbols and tell a physical map from a road or tourist map
Draw a simple plan of a classroom or a sketch map of the school surroundings
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} use a compass to find directions, read the symbols on a map, and draw a simple plan of their classroom?

topics.subject: Geography
topics.name: Position and Direction in Space
topics.description: Describing where things are with words such as left, right, above, behind and near; finding your way in a familiar room, school or street, and moving and turning your body as directed
evidence: Use position words (left, right, in front, behind, between) to say where something is
Follow and give simple directions in the classroom or school
Show on a simple drawing where they are and where something else is
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} give simple directions using words like left, right and behind to help someone find a place in school?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Generations and Family History
topics.description: Telling the past of one's family: grandparents, parents and children as generations, how daily life differed for older generations, and finding out about it from photos, objects and conversation
evidence: Name the generations in their family and order them in time
Describe one way daily life was different for an older generation
Use a photo, object or interview to find out something about the family's past
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell about their grandparents' or parents' childhood and say how it was different from theirs today?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Timelines and Historical Periods
topics.description: Using a timeline and a historical map to place events in order; recognising that a country's history is divided into periods with different ways of life, work and traditions; describing a few important events briefly
evidence: Place events on a timeline in the right order
Name some main periods of their country's history and tell one feature of each
Write a short text about one event from the past
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} put several historical events in order on a timeline and write a few sentences about one of them?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Public Holidays and Memorial Days
topics.description: Why societies have public holidays and memorial days (for example New Year, national days, labour day, days of remembrance), what each one marks, and how regional holidays differ
evidence: Name several public holidays of their country and what each marks
Explain why communities set aside shared days of celebration or remembrance
Describe how a holiday is observed in their family or region
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name several public holidays, say what each one marks, and explain why people observe them together?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: World Heritage and Protecting Monuments
topics.description: What World Heritage means: notable cultural monuments and natural sites in one's own and other countries, why they are protected, and simple ways a child can take part in protecting local heritage
evidence: Name two or three World Heritage cultural or natural sites
Explain why historic monuments and natural sites need protection
Suggest one way to help protect a monument or natural place nearby
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name a few World Heritage sites and explain why monuments and natural places are protected?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: Courtesy and Care for Others
topics.description: Good manners and conduct in society: attention and respect for others, including older people and people with disabilities, and the value of work to people and society
evidence: Show polite behaviour towards adults, peers and people who need extra help
Explain why respect for older people and people with disabilities matters
Describe how a person's work helps others
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe polite behaviour towards others, including people who need extra help, and explain why it matters?

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Safe Travel in the City
topics.description: Planning a safe route using the city's transport; safe conduct in public places and recreation areas; cycling and scooter safety with road signs, markings, signals and protective equipment
evidence: Plan a route that uses crossings and public transport sensibly
Explain safe conduct in public places such as parks, shops and theatres
Name key road signs and the protective gear and rules for cyclists and scooter riders
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} plan a safe route through a town and explain the basic rules for riding a bike or scooter near traffic?

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Finding, Judging and Presenting Information
topics.description: Using dictionaries, encyclopedias and the internet safely to find facts, judging how objective and reliable information is, and preparing a short report or presentation with pictures, tables or diagrams
evidence: Find an answer using a reference book or a safe web search
Judge whether a source seems objective and reliable, with a reason
Prepare a short report or slide presentation on a given topic
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} look up a topic in a reference source, judge whether the information is reliable, and make a short presentation about it?

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Planning and Checking My Own Work
topics.description: Planning the steps of a learning task, foreseeing difficulties and likely mistakes, checking progress, finding the cause of an error and correcting one's own actions
evidence: Write down the steps of a task before starting
Predict one difficulty or mistake that might happen
Find the cause of an error in their work and correct it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} plan the steps of a school task, anticipate a likely difficulty, and correct a mistake by finding its cause?

topics.subject: Geography
topics.name: Natural Zones and Their Living Things
topics.description: Natural zones of the Earth, such as tundra, forest, steppe and desert: sorting plants, animals and landscapes by the zone they belong to and noticing the gap between how a place is and how people would like it to be
evidence: Name several natural zones and locate them on a map
Sort plants and animals by the zone where they live
Describe a way a zone differs from what people want from it and what could be done
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name several natural zones and sort plants and animals by the zone they belong to?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: What a State Is
topics.description: What makes a state: territory, population, public authority, sovereignty, laws and symbols; the functions states carry out and the different forms a state can take
evidence: List the main features of a state and explain each
Describe the main functions a state performs for its people
Distinguish between a few forms of government with examples
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} list the main features of a state and describe what functions a state performs?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Branches of Government
topics.description: The idea of separating powers: lawmaking, executive and judicial bodies, what each does, how a law is made, and why dividing power helps prevent its misuse
evidence: Name the three branches and the task of each
Outline how a proposal becomes a law
Explain why dividing power between bodies matters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the branches of government, say what each does, and outline how a law is made?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: What a Constitution Is
topics.description: A constitution as the highest law of a state: what it contains (the structure of government, rights and duties), why it ranks above other laws, and how courts can check laws against it
evidence: Explain what a constitution is and what it usually contains
Say why a constitution ranks above ordinary laws
Give examples of rights and duties set out in a constitution
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a constitution is and why it ranks above ordinary laws?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Citizenship, Rights and Duties
topics.description: What citizenship is and how it is acquired; the basic rights and freedoms of people and citizens, the duties that go with them, and why rights and duties need balance
evidence: Explain what citizenship means and how people can obtain it
List basic rights and basic duties of citizens
Explain with an example why rights and duties go together
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what citizenship is and give examples of rights and duties that belong together?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Law, Norms and Legal Relations
topics.description: What law is: legal norms and branches of law, sources of law, legal relations with their subjects, objects and content, and the special legal position of minors
evidence: Explain how legal norms differ from other rules
Name sources and branches of law with examples
Describe the legal position of a minor in everyday situations
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how law differs from other rules and describe what a minor may and may not do legally?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Offences, Responsibility and Courts
topics.description: What an offence is and its kinds; legal liability and its types, how criminal liability of minors differs, and how courts and law enforcement bodies work
evidence: Distinguish an offence from other wrong behaviour with examples
Name types of legal liability and what each involves
Describe the roles of courts and law enforcement bodies
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what an offence is, name types of legal liability, and describe what courts and police do?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Everyday Official Procedures and Digital Services
topics.description: Handling everyday paperwork with public offices, including online government services, and the basics of student work, jobs and how occupations are changing
evidence: Name common matters that need an official procedure and where to handle them
Explain how an online public service works and its benefits
Describe basic legal conditions for a teenager's job and trends in occupations
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe how to handle a common official matter, including online, and the basic rules for a teenager taking a job?

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Consumer Rights
topics.description: What consumer protection covers, typical consumer rights and how to enforce them, the pros and risks of a consumer society, and informed shopping choices linked to sustainability
evidence: List consumer rights and where to turn if they are violated
Compare offers before buying and explain the choice
Give an example of how consumer choices affect the environment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name common consumer rights, say what to do after a faulty purchase, and compare offers before buying?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Education, Health and Welfare Systems
topics.description: The main public systems: education from school to higher and vocational training, health care and insurance, social support and family benefits; who works in them and why public service workers matter; student rights and duties
evidence: Outline the levels and parts of the education system and student rights and duties
Describe how health care and social support are organised
Explain why teachers, doctors and rescuers are important to society
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} outline how education, health care and social support are organised and explain what rights and duties a student has?

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: State, Taxes and the Budget
topics.description: How the state takes part in the economy: collecting taxes, the public budget, spending on public services, goals of economic policy, and why fair sharing of public burdens matters
evidence: Explain how taxes fund the public budget and services
Name areas of state economic activity
Discuss why paying taxes honestly matters to society
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how taxes pay for public budget spending and discuss why paying taxes matters?

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Markets, Money and Inflation
topics.description: Basic economics: economic goods, factors of production, property, exchange and trade, how markets set prices, the functions of money, inflation and the role of a central bank
evidence: Name economic goods and factors of production with examples
Explain how supply and demand shape a price
Describe functions of money, what inflation is and what a central bank does
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how markets set prices and what money, inflation and a central bank are?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: The Role of Science in Society
topics.description: How science develops society and everyday life, what frontier research looks like today and why public support for research matters
evidence: Give examples of how science changed everyday life
Describe an area of current research
Explain why research is publicly supported
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} give examples of how science has changed everyday life and explain why research needs support?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Culture and the Arts in Society
topics.description: What culture and cultural heritage are, kinds of art, the institutions that keep and present culture (museums, theatres, libraries), cultural policy, and the place of religion in culture
evidence: Explain what culture and cultural heritage mean with examples
Name kinds of art and cultural institutions
Describe the role of religion in the culture of a society
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what cultural heritage is and name kinds of art and the institutions that preserve them?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Debate and Dialogue in Society
topics.description: Expressing and supporting an opinion with arguments, listening to other views, and why respectful debate and dialogue between people and generations are useful to a community
evidence: State an opinion and support it with two reasons
Respond to a different view respectfully
Explain how debate helps a community make decisions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} state an opinion with reasons and respond respectfully to someone who disagrees?

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Computer Hardware Components
topics.description: The main parts of a computer and what each does: processor, working memory (RAM), long-term storage, input and output devices, and how phones, laptops, embedded computers and supercomputers differ
evidence: Name the processor, RAM, storage and input/output devices and say what each one does
Explain the difference between working memory and long-term storage
Compare a personal computer, a smartphone, an embedded computer and a supercomputer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the main parts inside a computer and explain what the processor, memory and storage each do?

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Using an Operating System and Apps
topics.description: Working with an operating system's interface: choosing the right device or app for a task, using settings and mobile school apps, and fixing simple user mistakes such as a frozen program or a lost window
evidence: Choose a suitable device or program for a given task and explain why
Use the desktop or mobile interface to open, switch and close apps and change basic settings
Solve a simple everyday problem (frozen app, no sound, full storage) by trying sensible steps
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} pick the right app or device for a task and sort out a simple problem, like a frozen program, without help?

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Types of Software and Licences
topics.description: Kinds of software: system software, applications and programming tools; how programs are protected by law, and the difference between paid, free trial and free open-source software
evidence: Sort programs into system software, application software and programming tools
Explain what a software licence is and why copying paid programs without permission is not allowed
Tell apart commercial, free trial and free open-source software with an example of each
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the difference between an operating system and an app, and between paid and free open-source software?

topics.subject: Computing
topics.name: Files, Folders and File Paths
topics.description: Organising data in files and folders: full file names and paths, creating, copying, moving, renaming, deleting and searching files, file types and sizes, and compressing files into archives
evidence: Read a file path and find the file it points to in a folder tree
Create, copy, move, rename and delete files and folders and find a file by searching

topics.subject: Computing

topics.subject: Mathematics

topics.subject: Computing

topics.subject: Life Skills

topics.subject: Life Skills

Put together a simple marketing plan with matching measures

topics.subject: Life Skills

topics.subject: Life Skills

Explain loan, interest and security with a small example
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how money developed and what it takes to borrow money, including interest?

topics.subject: Civics & Society
topics.name: Changing Social Roles and Equality Before the Law

Describe how floods are monitored and ways to protect water quality
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how people use and protect water resources and why water is unevenly available?

topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how the economic crisis and dictatorships changed Europe between the wars?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: World War II
topics.description: Causes and course of the war: aggression and crises of the 1930s, the Axis and Allies, main fronts in Europe and the Pacific, turning points, new methods of warfare and the end of the war
evidence: Explain the causes of World War II
Order the main events and turning points
Describe the Allied and Axis sides and fronts on a map
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how World War II began, what its turning points were and how it ended?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Persecution of Civilians and the Holocaust
topics.description: Racist persecution in Nazi-ruled Europe including the Holocaust, war crimes, suffering of civilians, occupation and forced deportations
evidence: Explain how persecution of Jews grew step by step
Describe how war affected civilians, including occupation and deportations
Explain why remembering these events matters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what the Holocaust was and how civilians suffered during the war?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The Cold War
topics.description: The post-war division of the world into two blocs, the arms race, the division of Germany, crises and conflicts in Korea and Cuba, and the United Nations
evidence: Explain what the Cold War was and who the two sides were
Describe the arms race and two crises
Explain what the United Nations was created to do
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what the Cold War was and name a few of its crises?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Decolonisation, Social Movements and Culture after 1945
topics.description: The end of colonial empires, movements for women's, minority and civil rights, peace movements, space exploration, mass media and popular culture
evidence: Explain why and how colonies became independent
Describe a rights movement and what it achieved
Name milestones of space exploration or media
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how colonies became independent and what rights movements asked for after 1945?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The World After the Cold War
topics.description: The fall of the Berlin Wall, changes in Eastern Europe, the dissolution of the USSR, the new political map of Europe, regional conflicts and international interventions
evidence: Order the main events of 1989–1991
Compare maps of Europe before and after
Explain how regional conflicts of the 1990s were handled internationally
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what happened in Europe in 1989–1991 and how the map changed?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: European Integration and the European Union
topics.description: From the Treaty of Rome to the Maastricht Treaty: the aims, enlargement, achievements and difficulties of the European Union and the euro
evidence: Explain why European states began to integrate
Order key steps from 1957 to the present
Describe benefits and difficulties of the Union
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why the European Union was created and how it has grown?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Globalisation and the Digital Age
topics.description: Global trade and migration, the Fourth Industrial Revolution with the internet, social networks and mobile phones, and how these changed work, media and daily life
evidence: Define globalisation and give examples
Describe how digital technology changed communication
Discuss benefits and risks of digital media
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what globalisation is and how the internet changed everyday life?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Population and Society Through History
topics.description: Food production and settled life, limits on population growth, the plague, population explosion with industrialisation, urbanisation, migration and changing roles of women
evidence: Describe main periods of population change
Explain causes and effects of population growth or decline
Compare traditional and industrial societies
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how and why human population and society changed from farming times to the industrial age?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Origins and the Árpád-era Kingdom of Hungary
topics.description: Medieval accounts of the Hungarians' origins (Hunor and Magor, Emese's dream), the Conquest of the Carpathian Basin in 895, the founding of the kingdom under King Stephen I, the Golden Bull of 1222 and the Mongol invasion

Describe the Conquest and the founding of the kingdom with key dates
Name rulers of the Árpád dynasty and one thing each did
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell the main events from the Conquest of 895 to the Mongol invasion of 1241?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Hungary in the Ottoman Wars
topics.description: The Battle of Mohács in 1526, the fall of Buda and the division of the country into three parts, the siege heroes (Dobó, Zrínyi), life under Ottoman rule in market towns and cattle trade, and the Baroque era
evidence: Explain why the country was divided into three parts
Describe a siege and its defenders
Describe daily life in a market town under Ottoman rule
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what happened at Mohács and how the country was divided in the 16th century?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The Hungarian Reform Era and 1848
topics.description: The reform era of the 1820s–40s (Széchenyi's projects, the emancipation of serfs, Hungarian language and culture), the revolution and war of independence of 1848–49, and the later Compromise
evidence: Name reforms proposed in the Reform Era and who proposed them
Describe the main events of 1848–49
Explain why the Compromise followed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what the Reform Era aimed to change and what happened in 1848–49?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Austria-Hungary and the Dualist Era
topics.description: The 1867 Compromise and the dual monarchy with common affairs, railways and river regulation, industry and inventions, the growth of Budapest, the 1896 Millennium and emancipation
evidence: Explain what dualism meant and which affairs were common
Give examples of modernisation in Hungary
Describe how Budapest grew into a metropolis
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what changed in Hungary after the Compromise of 1867?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Hungary in World War I and the Trianon Treaty
topics.description: Hungarians in the war and on the home front, the revolutions of 1918–19, the Treaty of Trianon of 1920 and its territorial, population and economic consequences
evidence: Describe Hungary's role in the war and the situation at home
Explain what the Treaty of Trianon decided
Compare maps of Hungary before and after 1920
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what the Treaty of Trianon decided and what it changed for Hungary?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Hungary 1920–1945: The Horthy Era and World War II
topics.description: The Horthy era: the regent, Bethlen's consolidation, revision efforts, antisemitic laws, Klebelsberg's education policy, culture and science; then Hungary's alliances, the war and its consequences
evidence: Describe politics, economy and culture of the 1920s–30s
Identify antisemitic measures from sources
Explain why Hungary entered the war and what followed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe the main features of the Horthy era and Hungary's path into World War II?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Hungary under Communist Rule, 1945–1989
topics.description: Soviet occupation, expulsions and deportations, elections of 1945 and 1947, the one-party dictatorship of 1948–56, the revolution of October 1956 and its suppression, the Kádár era, and the change of system in 1989–90
evidence: Describe how a one-party system was built after 1945
Describe the main events of the 1956 revolution
Explain how the change of system of 1989–90 happened
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what happened in Hungary in 1956 and how the communist system ended?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Peoples and Minorities of the Carpathian Basin
topics.description: Turning points in the history of Hungarian communities outside Hungary since 1920, minority life and assimilation, ethnic maps of 1910 and after 1990, and examples of cooperation and conflict among the peoples of the region
evidence: Compare ethnic maps of the basin in 1910 and after 1990
Describe challenges of minority life with examples
Give examples of cooperation among neighbouring peoples
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how borders changed in the Carpathian Basin and what that meant for minority communities?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Hungarians in Science, Arts and Sport Worldwide
topics.description: Notable Hungarian travellers and explorers, scientists and inventors, Olympic athletes and artists who worked at home and abroad
evidence: Name Hungarian scientists, inventors or explorers and their work
Name Hungarian Olympic successes
Present one Hungarian artist or scientist
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} present a few Hungarian scientists, inventors, athletes or artists and what they achieved?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Serbian Lands in the Early Middle Ages
topics.description: The settlement of Serbs and Croats in the Balkans, relations with older inhabitants and neighbours, the formation of Serbian lands, Christianisation, the spread of literacy and the work of Cyril and Methodius
evidence: Describe how the Slavs settled in the Balkans
Explain how Christianity and literacy reached Serbian lands
Explain the work of Cyril and Methodius
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how Serbian lands formed and how Christianity and writing came to them?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The Serbian Revolution and the Principality of Serbia
topics.description: Life of Serbs under Ottoman and Habsburg rule, the First and Second Serbian Uprisings, 1804–1835, the autonomous Principality under Prince Miloš and the founding of schools and cultural institutions
evidence: Explain causes and course of the two uprisings
Describe the autonomy of the Principality and its institutions
Name key people such as Karađorđe, Miloš, Dositej Obradović and Vuk Karadžić
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how the Serbian uprisings led to the autonomous Principality of Serbia?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Serbia in the Second Half of the 19th and Early 20th Centuries
topics.description: The development of state institutions and political life, international recognition at the Congress of Berlin, the Kingdom of Serbia, the coup of 1903, Montenegro's constitution and kingdom, and the Balkan Wars
evidence: Describe institutions and political life of the Principality and Kingdom of Serbia
Explain what the Congress of Berlin decided for Serbia
Describe the aims and results of the Balkan Wars
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how Serbia became an internationally recognised kingdom and what the Balkan Wars changed?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Serbia and Montenegro in the Great War
topics.description: Serbia and Montenegro in World War I: fronts and key battles, losses, hunger and epidemics, life under occupation and in exile, and remembrance of the war
evidence: Describe the role of Serbia and Montenegro in the war
Describe the situation of civilians under occupation and in exile
Explain how the war is remembered
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe what happened to Serbia and Montenegro in World War I and how civilians lived?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Creation of Yugoslavia and the Interwar Kingdom
topics.description: The Yugoslav idea, how and by whom the state was formed in 1918, its borders and recognition, and politics, economy, culture and national and religious questions in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia
evidence: Explain the Yugoslav idea and how the state was formed in 1918
Describe the political and economic situation of the kingdom
Name national and religious questions debated in the interwar state
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how Yugoslavia was formed in 1918 and what the main issues of the interwar state were?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Yugoslavia in World War II
topics.description: Entry into the war, military defeat, occupation and partition of the country, resistance movements and the civil conflict, suffering of civilians and war crimes, and the end of the war
evidence: Describe how Yugoslavia entered the war and was occupied
