Name the resistance movements and the conflicts among them
Describe the suffering of civilians and the end of the war
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe what happened to Yugoslavia during World War II?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Socialist Yugoslavia
topics.description: Reconstruction and the building of the post-war federal state, its place in a divided world, economy and social change, culture and daily life
evidence: Describe the post-war reconstruction and the structure of the federation
Explain Yugoslavia's position between the two Cold War blocs
Describe changes in economy and daily life
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe how Yugoslavia was organised after 1945 and where it stood in the Cold War?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Dissolution of Yugoslavia and Serbia Today
topics.description: The crisis of the 1980s, introduction of multi-party systems, the dissolution of the federation, the wars of the 1990s and their consequences for civilians and cultural heritage, political changes of 2000 and relations in the region
evidence: Order key events from the 1980s crisis to 2000
Describe consequences of the wars for people and heritage
Explain how regional relations and the EU accession process have developed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} order the main events from the crisis of the 1980s to the political changes of 2000 and describe their consequences?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Folk tales and their features
topics.description: Recognise folk tales by their typical features: 'once upon a time' openings, repeated actions in threes, magical helpers, clear good and bad characters and a happy or just ending
evidence: Name at least three typical features of folk tales, e.g. 'three tasks', a magical helper, a fixed opening
Tell which of two stories is a folk tale and which is a modern story, and say why
Retell a folk tale keeping its repeated patterns and ending
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} listen to a folk tale and point out typical features such as a magical helper, things happening three times or a traditional opening?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Folk songs and historical songs
topics.description: Folk songs as anonymous songs passed on by singing: lullabies, work songs, lyrical songs and historical songs that remember events, with refrains and repeated lines
evidence: Tell a lyrical folk song from a historical or work song by what it is about
Point out refrains, repeated lines and simple images (a bird, a river, a tree) in a folk song
Explain that folk songs have no single known author and change as people pass them on
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what makes a folk song different from a song with a known composer, using refrains and repeated lines as examples?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Myths and legends
topics.description: Myths and legends as old stories about gods, heroes and the origin of the world or of customs: how a myth explains nature, and how a legend mixes real places or people with wonder
evidence: Tell a myth from a legend and from a fairy tale, giving one reason
Explain what a given myth tries to explain, e.g. thunder, seasons or the origin of fire
Name a god or hero from the myths of at least two cultures and what they stand for
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} retell a myth or legend and explain what question about the world or about people it tries to answer?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Epic poetry and heroic songs
topics.description: Epic poems and heroic songs that tell of great deeds of a hero in long, solemn verse with fixed epithets, repeated formulas and exaggeration, such as the Iliad, the Odyssey or medieval heroic songs
evidence: Describe what makes a poem an epic: a hero, great deeds, a long story told in verse
Find fixed epithets, repeated phrases and exaggeration in an epic passage
Explain that epics were first performed aloud and handed down by singers before being written
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what an epic poem is and spot features such as a hero, fixed epithets or exaggeration in a short passage?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian byliny
topics.description: Russian byliny: heroic folk songs about knights such as Ilya Muromets and the merchant Sadko, sung in a chant-like verse with a slow opening, repeated formulas and magical enemies
evidence: Name a bylina hero and one deed he performs
Recognise bylina features such as a slow, ceremonial opening, repetition and exaggerated strength
Compare a bylina hero with a hero of a folk tale
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} retell a bylina and point out features such as exaggerated strength, repetition and a ceremonial opening?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Serbian epic folk songs
topics.description: Serbian epic folk songs sung to the gusle: songs of the Kosovo cycle, of Marko Kraljević and of outlaws (hajduks) in the ten-syllable verse, with fixed epithets and a heroic or tragic tone
evidence: Name a song cycle (e.g. about Marko Kraljević or the hajduks) and one of its characters
Recognise the ten-syllable verse, fixed epithets and the singer's formulas in a passage
Explain what the songs were for: they carried memory and values by being sung with the gusle
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} retell a Serbian epic folk song and point out its ten-syllable lines and fixed epithets?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Old Russian literature
topics.description: The earliest Russian writing: chronicle stories, teachings and tales (such as the Primary Chronicle and the Tale of Igor's Campaign), with their purpose, style and the way they record events
evidence: Name two kinds of old Russian writing, e.g. a chronicle entry and a teaching
Explain how a chronicle tells events year by year and for what purpose
Point out how the language and imagery of an old text differ from modern writing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a chronicle or a teaching from Old Russian literature is and how it differs from a modern story?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Lives of saints
topics.description: Lives of saints (hagiography) as a medieval genre: a standard plan of birth, youth, deeds and death, written to give an example of conduct, and how it differs from a biography
evidence: Describe the usual parts of a saint's life as a text
Explain how a saint's life differs from a modern biography in purpose and style
Identify a story or legend in a given text that serves as a moral example
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how a saint's life differs from an ordinary biography in purpose and structure?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Literary tales and folk tales
topics.description: How a literary tale by a known author differs from a folk tale: an individual style, original characters and plot, borrowed folk motifs, and the role of illustrations
evidence: Say who made up a literary tale and how it can differ from a folk tale
Find folk motifs (a magical helper, three tries) in a literary tale
Describe how pictures in a tale add to the story
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} compare a literary tale with a folk tale and tell what the author added?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Fables: animal characters and allegory
topics.description: A fable is a short story, in prose or verse, in which animals act like people to show a human fault or virtue; the lesson (moral) is stated or implied
evidence: Say what human quality each animal in a fable stands for
State the moral of a fable in one sentence
Tell a fable from an ordinary animal story
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a fable's animals stand for and state its moral?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Short story: theme, characters and composition
topics.description: Features of a short story: the theme, the characters and how they are described (portrait, setting), the order of events (opening, build-up, climax, ending) and what is real in the events
evidence: State the theme of a short story in a sentence
Describe how the author shows a character (looks, actions, words)
Place events on a simple plot line from beginning to ending
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the theme of a short story and describe how the author shows a main character?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Humour in stories
topics.description: How authors make a story funny: comic situations, exaggeration, funny names and speech, and the difference between laughing with a character and laughing at them
evidence: Point out what makes a passage funny: a situation, exaggeration or the way someone talks
Tell the difference between a gentle joke and a mocking one
Retell a funny story keeping the comic moment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what makes a funny story funny, e.g. exaggeration or a comic situation?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Stories about animals and nature
topics.description: Stories where animals and the natural world are the subject: how authors show an animal's character, the bond between people and animals, and care for nature
evidence: Describe how an author shows an animal's behaviour and character
Explain what a story says about people's responsibility to animals and nature
Tell a realistic animal story from a fantasy one
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a story about an animal tells us about the animal and about how people treat nature?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Adventure, fantasy and science fiction
topics.description: Genres of invented worlds and daring journeys: adventure stories (travel, danger, survival), fantasy and science fiction (imagined worlds, inventions, the future), and what each asks of the reader
evidence: Tell an adventure story from a fantasy or science-fiction story and say why
Identify what is invented (a place, creature or technology) in such a story
Describe the main challenge a hero faces and how it is solved
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell adventure, fantasy and science fiction apart and name what is invented in a given story?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Historical fiction and stories of war
topics.description: Fiction set in a real past: how an author blends real events and invented characters, and how stories of war show the experience of ordinary people, including children, and its consequences
evidence: Tell which parts of a historical story are real events and which are invented
Describe how a character's life is changed by events of the period
Explain how a story conveys the human cost of war without using details of violence
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell the real events from the invented characters in a historical story and describe how events changed a character's life?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Coming-of-age stories
topics.description: Stories of growing up: a young character meets a first loss, friendship, conflict or moral choice and changes; reading how the author shows inner change in thoughts and actions
evidence: Describe how a main character changes between the start and end of a story
Name the event that starts the change and explain why it matters
Link the character's feelings to what they do
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how a character in a coming-of-age story grows or changes and which event caused it?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Autobiography and memoir
topics.description: Texts in which an author tells about their own life: how an autobiography or memoir uses 'I', real events and memory, and how it differs from a novel or a biography written by someone else
evidence: Tell an autobiography from a biography and a novel
Find the 'I' voice and the real events in a passage
Explain how a memory is shaped by the person who tells it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how an autobiography differs from a biography written by another person?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Story, novella and novel
topics.description: Prose forms by length and scope: the short story with one event, the novella (povest) with a longer plot and several characters, and the novel with many storylines and a wider world
evidence: Order a short story, a novella and a novel by scope and say why
Describe how a longer work can have several storylines and characters
Pick the right word (story, novella, novel) for a text they have read
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how a short story, a novella and a novel differ in length and plot?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Satire and parody
topics.description: Satire shows human or social faults through humour, exaggeration and irony so that readers see them clearly; parody imitates another work or style to make fun of it
evidence: Explain what fault a satirical text is aiming at
Find exaggeration or irony used for satire in a passage
Tell a parody from the work it imitates
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a satirical text is poking fun at and how exaggeration helps?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Irony and unexpected endings
topics.description: Irony is a gap between what is said or expected and what happens; a short story can end with a twist that makes the reader see the whole story differently
evidence: Describe the twist at the end of a short story and what the reader expected
Tell the difference between what a character says and what the author means
Explain how a surprise ending changes the meaning of earlier events
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} point out irony or a surprise ending in a short story and explain how it changes the meaning?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Symbol and allegory in fiction
topics.description: A symbol is an object, place or character that stands for an idea (a rose, a road, a ship); an allegorical story carries a second meaning beneath the plot, as in a fable-like tale for older readers
evidence: Name a symbol in a story and say what it stands for
Explain the second meaning of a short allegorical tale
Tell the literal level of a story from its symbolic level
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name a symbol in a story and explain what idea it stands for?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Social themes in literature
topics.description: How literature shows life in a society: work, poverty, inequality, duty and kindness; reading a story or poem for what it shows about the lives of ordinary people in its time
evidence: Describe the living conditions of a character as shown in a text
Explain how the author's attitude to the character can be inferred
Link the situation in a text to the time in which it was written
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe what a story or poem shows about the life of ordinary people in its time and what the author seems to feel about it?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Storyteller's voice (skaz)
topics.description: A story told in the lively voice of a narrator who speaks like an ordinary person, with sayings, dialect words and jokes (skaz), so the way of telling is part of the meaning
evidence: Notice words and sayings that make a narrator sound like a particular person
Tell the narrator's voice from the author's voice
Retell a short passage in a different narrator's voice
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} point out how a narrator's way of speaking, with its sayings and special words, shapes a story?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Landscape and place in prose and poetry
topics.description: How writers describe landscapes, seasons and home places to create mood: choice of details, colours, sounds and comparisons, and why a place may matter to a character or speaker
evidence: Pick out the details that build a picture of a place in a text
Describe the mood of a description of nature
Write or say a short description of a place using concrete details and one comparison
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} point out the details a writer uses to describe a landscape and say what mood they create?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Authors and their time
topics.description: How an author's life and the period they lived in shape a work: why a writer chose a subject, what the text shows about its time, and how the same work can be read differently today
evidence: Link one fact about an author's life or time to something in their text
Describe what a text reveals about everyday life in its period
Explain why readers of a different time may understand a work differently
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} link something in a text to the author's life or the period when it was written?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Translated literature and translators
topics.description: Many books are read in translation: a translator re-tells a work in another language, choosing words and rhymes, so two translations of one text can sound different
evidence: Say that a book was written in another language and translated
Compare two short translations of a sentence or verse and name a difference
Explain why translating a rhyme or a joke is hard
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a translator does and why two translations of one text can differ?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Moral choices and heroic deeds in stories
topics.description: Telling a deed (an action with a clear motive) from a brave or generous act; explaining why a character chose as they did and what this shows about their values
evidence: Describe a character's deed and the reason behind it
Explain what makes an act brave, kind or unselfish in a text
Say whether they would have chosen the same and why
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe a character's brave or kind deed and explain why the character acted that way?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: The lyric poem: speaker and mood
topics.description: A lyric poem expresses a feeling or thought through a speaker's voice; reading for the speaker, the mood, the central image and how the title and the last lines shape the meaning
evidence: Say who is speaking in a poem and what they feel
Name the central image and what it adds
Explain how the mood changes between the first and last stanza
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} say who is speaking in a poem, what the mood is and which images create it?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Rhyme and stanza
topics.description: Rhyming lines and the way a poem is built in lines and stanzas: finding rhyming pairs, seeing the pattern of rhymes (AABB, ABAB), and counting lines in a stanza
evidence: Find rhyming words at the ends of lines in a poem
Mark the rhyme pattern of a four-line stanza
Count the lines and stanzas in a poem
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the rhymes in a poem and tell how many lines and stanzas it has?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Verse metre and rhythm
topics.description: How the pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables gives a poem its rhythm: marking stress in a line, naming the basic feet (iamb, trochee, dactyl, amphibrach, anapaest) and counting feet per line
evidence: Mark stressed and unstressed syllables in a line of verse
Name the metre (e.g. iambic or trochaic) of a short passage
Explain how a change in rhythm can change the feel of a line
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} mark the stresses in a line of verse and name its metre, such as iambic or trochaic?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Epithet, personification and hyperbole
topics.description: Three ways to make description vivid: an epithet (a descriptive adjective like 'golden autumn'), personification (giving things human traits) and hyperbole (deliberate exaggeration)
evidence: Find an epithet in a line and say what it adds
Explain which human trait is given to a thing in personification
Spot hyperbole and say what it emphasises
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} spot an epithet, a personification and a hyperbole in a poem or story and explain the effect?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Sound devices in poetry
topics.description: How the sound of words adds meaning in verse: alliteration (repeated consonants), assonance (repeated vowels) and onomatopoeia, and how they imitate sounds or set a mood
evidence: Find alliteration or assonance in a line and read it aloud for effect
Name an onomatopoeic word and the sound it imitates
Explain what mood repeated sounds create (soft, harsh, fast)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find repeated sounds in a poem and say what effect they have?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Narrative poems and ballads
topics.description: Poems that tell a story: a ballad or a longer narrative poem (poem, poema) with a plot, characters and a narrator in verse, and how verse and storytelling work together
evidence: Tell a narrative poem from a lyric poem
Retell the plot of a narrative poem in order
Explain what the verse form adds to the telling, e.g. rhythm or refrain
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} retell the story of a narrative poem or ballad and say what the verse adds?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Parts of a play: dialogue, stage directions and acts
topics.description: How a play is written: characters' lines in dialogue, stage directions (remarks) about movement and setting, and the division into scenes and acts
evidence: Tell speech from stage directions in a script
Describe what a stage direction tells an actor
Say how a play is divided into scenes and acts
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} point out dialogue and stage directions in a script and say what each is for?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Comedy as a dramatic genre
topics.description: A comedy is a play that treats faults and funny situations lightly: comic characters, misunderstandings, mistaken identity, and an ending that restores order
evidence: Name features that make a play a comedy
Explain what fault or weakness a comic character shows
Describe how a misunderstanding drives the plot of a comedy
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what makes a play a comedy and name a comic character's weakness?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Staging a scene: reading by roles and acting
topics.description: Preparing a short scene: reading a text by roles, using voice, pace and gesture, and following the rules of working together while rehearsing and performing
evidence: Read a scene by roles with a fitting voice
Act out a short scene using movement and gesture
Take turns and listen to partners during rehearsal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} read a short scene by roles and act it out with others, listening to partners and taking turns?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Reading goals and self-assessment
topics.description: Setting a small reading task (what to read, how much), keeping at it, asking for help when stuck, and saying in simple words what went well and what was hard in own reading
evidence: Keep a reading task in mind until it is done
Ask a teacher or parent for help when a text is too hard
Say what went well and what was hard in own reading
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} keep a reading task in mind, ask for help when stuck and say what went well in their own reading?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Sounds and Letters
topics.description: Telling a sound (what we hear and say) from a letter (what we write), and sorting sounds into vowels and consonants, e.g. the word "sun" has three sounds
evidence: Explain that sounds are heard and spoken while letters are written
Sort the sounds of a short word into vowels and consonants
Find a word where the number of letters and sounds differs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the difference between a sound and a letter and say which sounds in a short word are vowels?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Sound Analysis of Words
topics.description: Analysing a word step by step: say it slowly, count syllables and sounds, mark stress, describe each sound and match sounds to letters, e.g. "ice" has three letters and three sounds
evidence: Say a word slowly and count its sounds and syllables
Mark the stressed syllable and describe each sound as vowel or consonant
Write a sound-by-letter scheme of a word and check it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} take a short word apart sound by sound, draw a simple scheme of it and check that each sound has its letter?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Hard and Soft, Voiced and Voiceless Consonants
topics.description: Describing consonant sounds by pairs: hard-soft and voiced-voiceless, and knowing which consonants have no pair, e.g. [b]-[p], [d]-[t] or Russian [р] and [р']
evidence: Name the pairs of voiced and voiceless consonants
Tell whether a consonant in a word is hard or soft
Give a full description of a consonant sound (voiced/voiceless, hard/soft, paired/unpaired)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe a consonant sound in a word as voiced or voiceless and hard or soft, and say whether it has a pair?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian Soft and Hard Signs and Iotated Letters
topics.description: How Russian letters ь, ъ, е, ё, ю, я work: ь showing softness or separating, ъ separating, and е ё ю я giving two sounds at the start of a word or after a vowel, e.g. семья, объезд
evidence: Explain three jobs of the soft sign (softness, separation, none at the end of some words)
Choose ь or ъ as a separating sign in a word
Say how many sounds are in words with е, ё, ю, я such as "ёлка"
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what the Russian letters ь and ъ do in a word and count sounds in words with е, ё, ю, я?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Syllables and Word Division
topics.description: Dividing words into syllables by counting vowels, and using this to break a word at the end of a line, e.g. "ma-chine"; knowing that a one-letter syllable should not be left alone
evidence: Count the syllables in a word by its vowels
Divide a word into syllables, including words with several consonants in a row
Split a word correctly at a line end with a hyphen
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} divide a word into syllables and choose a correct place to break it at the end of a written line?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Word Stress and Standard Pronunciation
topics.description: Hearing which syllable is stressed, using a pronunciation dictionary to check how a word is said, and following the norms of standard speech, e.g. Russian звонИт, тортЫ
evidence: Find the stressed syllable in a word
Check stress and pronunciation of a doubtful word in a dictionary
Pronounce and stress words from a school list in the standard way
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the stressed syllable in a word and look up the standard pronunciation of a word in a dictionary?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian Spelling Rules for Hushing Consonants
topics.description: Applying spelling rules for sound combinations in Russian: жи–ши with и, ча–ща with а, чу–щу with у, and чк, чн without a soft sign, e.g. шило, чаща, булочная
evidence: State the rules жи–ши, ча–ща, чу–щу
Fill in the right letter in words with these combinations
Write words with чк and чн correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} spell Russian words with жи–ши, ча–ща, чу–щу, чк and чн correctly and say which rule applies?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Words with Unverifiable Spelling
topics.description: Learning words whose spelling cannot be worked out by a rule, and checking them in a spelling dictionary, e.g. Russian "собака", "ворона", English "friend"
evidence: Recognise that a word's spelling cannot be checked by a rule
Look up the word in a spelling dictionary or word list
Memorise and write a set of such words correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} spot a word whose spelling has to be memorised and check it in a spelling dictionary?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Copying and Writing from Dictation
topics.description: Copying a text accurately and writing words and short sentences from dictation, then checking and correcting mistakes, e.g. reading a sentence, dividing it into words and writing it with spelling marked
evidence: Copy a sentence correctly, word by word
Write a short text from dictation, applying learned rules
Find and correct own mistakes after checking
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} copy a short text without errors and write a few sentences from dictation, then find and fix their own mistakes?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Spaces, Paragraphs and Punctuation as Text Signs
topics.description: Knowing the non-letter signs that organise writing: word spaces, the hyphen for line breaks, paragraph indent and punctuation marks, e.g. a red line starts a new paragraph
evidence: Leave proper spaces between words
Start a new paragraph with an indent
Name basic punctuation marks and say what they show
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} show where a paragraph begins in a text and name the punctuation marks used in it?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian Unstressed Case Endings
topics.description: Choosing the right vowel in unstressed case endings of Russian nouns and adjectives by finding the declension and the case, e.g. в реке, к сестре, о красивой книге
evidence: Determine the declension and case of a noun
Choose е or и in unstressed noun endings by the rule
Check endings of adjectives by asking the question and using a stressed ending
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} choose the correct unstressed ending of a Russian noun or adjective by working out its case and declension?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian Soft Sign After Hushing Consonants and in Verbs
topics.description: Writing ь after ж, ч, ш, щ at the end of nouns and verbs, and in verb endings -ться/-тся and -ешь, e.g. рожь, ночь, учишь, учится, учиться
evidence: Write ь after hushing consonants in nouns of the 3rd declension but not in the 2nd
Distinguish -тся and -ться by asking the question
Write ь in the 2nd person singular of verbs (-ешь, -ишь)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} decide when to write a soft sign after a hushing consonant and tell apart -тся and -ться in Russian verbs?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Parts of Speech
topics.description: Grouping words by what they mean and how they change: nouns, adjectives, verbs, pronouns, numerals, adverbs, and function words, e.g. "table" (thing), "red" (feature), "run" (action)
evidence: Name the main parts of speech and the question each answers
Sort a list of words into parts of speech
Explain why a word belongs to a part of speech using its meaning and forms
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} sort words from a sentence into parts of speech and explain why each belongs there?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian Noun Cases and Declensions
topics.description: Changing Russian nouns by six cases and three declensions, in singular and plural, including nouns in -мя, -ий, -ие, -ия, -ья and indeclinable nouns, e.g. книга-книги, дом-домов, пальто
evidence: Name the six cases and their questions
Assign a noun to its declension
Decline a noun in singular and plural and spot an indeclinable noun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} decline a Russian noun by cases, say which declension it belongs to and recognise nouns that do not change?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Kinds of Adjectives and Degrees of Comparison
topics.description: Telling qualitative, relative and possessive adjectives apart and forming the comparative and superlative of quality adjectives, e.g. добрый-добрее-добрейший, wooden, mother's
evidence: Sort adjectives into qualitative, relative and possessive
Form comparative and superlative forms
Explain how an adjective is related to its noun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} sort adjectives into qualitative, relative and possessive kinds and form their degrees of comparison?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Numerals
topics.description: Words that name numbers: cardinal and ordinal, simple, compound and collective numerals, how they change and how they are spelled, e.g. three, third, two hundred, Hungarian harminc, harmincadik
evidence: Tell cardinal numerals from ordinals
Write compound numerals correctly (spaces, hyphen or one word as the language requires)
Use a numeral in the right form with a noun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} identify numerals in a sentence, tell cardinal from ordinal and write them correctly?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Kinds of Pronouns and Their Use
topics.description: Pronouns that replace nouns, adjectives or numerals: personal, reflexive, interrogative, relative, demonstrative, possessive, indefinite, negative and defining, and their forms in different cases
evidence: Name kinds of pronouns and give an example of each
Decline a personal pronoun
Use pronouns so that it is clear who or what is meant
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the kinds of pronouns in a text and use them so the meaning stays clear?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian Participles
topics.description: A special verb form that names a feature by action and agrees like an adjective, including н and нн in suffixes and spelling of не with participles, e.g. написанный, читающий
evidence: Recognise a participle in a sentence and its question
Choose н or нн in participles and verbal adjectives
Decide whether не is written together or apart
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find participles in a sentence and write н/нн and не with them correctly?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian Adverbial Participles
topics.description: A verb form that names an extra action, does not change and is set off by commas, in perfective and imperfective form, with vowels in suffixes and не written apart, e.g. читая, прочитав
evidence: Find an adverbial participle and the action it shows
Form it from a verb with the correct suffix
Put commas around it and write не apart
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find and form adverbial participles in Russian and punctuate them correctly?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Adverbs
topics.description: Words that tell how, where, when or how much an action happens, which do not change except in degrees of comparison, and their spelling, e.g. quickly, here, tomorrow, Russian по-новому, вдали
evidence: Find adverbs and say what they answer (how, where, when)
Form degrees of comparison of adverbs
Spell adverbs: together, apart or with a hyphen
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find adverbs in a sentence, say what they tell about the action and spell tricky ones correctly?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Function Words, Particles and Interjections
topics.description: Words that do not name things but link or colour speech: prepositions, conjunctions, particles (forming, negative, modal) and interjections, with words of state, e.g. Russian бы, ли, же, -то, ах, ура
evidence: Tell independent parts of speech from function words
Name the job of a particle (shade of meaning, negation, forming a mood)
Punctuate an interjection and recognise sound-imitating words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} point out particles, conjunctions and interjections in a text and say what each does?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Russian не and ни Spelling
topics.description: Distinguishing the particle не from the prefix не- and from ни, and writing не together or apart with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs and participles, e.g. невысокий, не высокий, а низкий; никто, не кто-то
evidence: Tell the meaning of не and ни
Decide together/apart spelling with different parts of speech
Explain the choice using a rule
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} choose the correct spelling of Russian не and ни with different parts of speech and explain the rule?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Word Formation
topics.description: How new words are made from existing ones: adding prefixes and suffixes, joining stems to form compounds, and changing the part of speech, e.g. teach-teacher, rail+road, Russian пароход, run-runner
evidence: Name the ways of forming words (prefix, suffix, compounding)
Build a new word from a given one and say how it was made
Write compound words correctly (together or with a hyphen)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how a given word was formed and make new words from it by adding parts or joining words?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Phrases
topics.description: Word combinations made of a main and a dependent word, types of connection and how the same idea can be said in different ways, e.g. "red apple", "read a book", "reading of books"
evidence: Find the main and the dependent word in a phrase
Name the type of connection (agreement, government, adjoining)
Replace a phrase with a synonymous one
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} pick out phrases from a sentence and say which word is the main one?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Subject and Predicate
topics.description: The grammatical basis of a sentence: the subject says who or what, the predicate says what it does or is, with simple verbal, compound verbal and compound nominal predicates, e.g. "The dog barks", "Moscow is a city"
evidence: Find the subject and the predicate
Name the kind of predicate
Say how the subject and predicate agree, including the dash in Russian
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the subject and predicate in a sentence and say what kind of predicate it is?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Attributes and Apposition
topics.description: The secondary sentence part that describes a noun: agreeing and non-agreeing attributes and apposition as a special kind, e.g. "a deep river", "the city of Kazan", "river Volga"
evidence: Find the attribute and the noun it describes
Tell agreeing from non-agreeing attributes
Find an apposition
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the words that describe a noun in a sentence and name their kind?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Objects and Adverbial Modifiers
topics.description: Secondary sentence parts: objects (direct and indirect) answering case questions, and adverbials of place, time, cause, purpose, manner, degree, condition and concession, e.g. "read a book", "go home", "because of rain"
evidence: Find direct and indirect objects
Name the kind of adverbial by its question
Ask a question from the verb to each secondary part
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find objects and adverbials in a sentence and say whether they show place, time, cause or manner?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: One-Part Sentences in Russian
topics.description: Russian sentences with only one main member: nominative, definite-personal, indefinite-personal, generalised-personal and impersonal, e.g. Ночь., Иду домой., Говорят., Темнеет.
evidence: Find the main member of a one-part sentence
Name its kind
Tell a one-part sentence from an incomplete two-part one
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} identify a Russian one-part sentence and say which kind it is?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Incomplete Sentences and Word Order
topics.description: Sentences where a part is left out because the context makes it clear, especially in dialogue, and the effect of changing word order, e.g. "Where are you going?" - "Home."
evidence: Find the missing part of a sentence from context
Use incomplete sentences in dialogue with the right intonation
Change word order to stress a different word
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} spot an incomplete sentence in a dialogue and say which part is missing?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Homogeneous Sentence Parts
topics.description: Equal sentence parts answering the same question and joined by commas or conjunctions, with generalising words, e.g. "She bought apples, pears and plums"; commas with but/and/not only... but also
evidence: Find homogeneous parts in a sentence
Put commas between them correctly
Punctuate a generalising word before the list
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find sentence parts of the same kind in a sentence and place the commas correctly?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Set-Off and Clarifying Sentence Parts
topics.description: Sentence parts that are set apart in speech and with commas because they add detail: attributes, appositions, adverbials and objects, and clarifying members, e.g. "The boy, tired after the walk, fell asleep"
evidence: Find a set-off part in a sentence
Put commas or dashes around it
Explain why the part is set off
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find a part of a sentence that is set off by commas and explain why?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Direct Address
topics.description: Words naming the person or thing we speak to, not part of the sentence structure and set off by commas or an exclamation, e.g. "Mum, come here!", "Dear friends, ..."
evidence: Find a direct address in a sentence
Punctuate it correctly at start, middle or end
Extend an address with describing words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the word naming who is spoken to and punctuate it correctly?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Introductory and Inserted Constructions
topics.description: Words and phrases showing the speaker's attitude, certainty, source or order of thoughts, or adding side remarks, set off by commas or brackets, e.g. "of course", "in my opinion", "first of all"
evidence: Find an introductory word in a sentence and tell what it shows
Separate it from words that look alike but are sentence parts
Punctuate an inserted remark
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find an introductory word in a sentence and tell whether it is separated by commas?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Compound Sentences
topics.description: Sentences made of equal clauses joined by conjunctions such as and, but, or, with meaning relations between the parts and the right intonation and commas, e.g. "The sun set, and it became cold"
evidence: Find the clauses of a compound sentence
Name the meaning relation (adding, contrast, choice)
Place commas and replace a compound sentence with a simple one
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the clauses of a compound sentence, name the conjunction and punctuate it?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Meaning of Words
topics.description: A word is sound plus meaning: finding what a word means, spotting words whose meaning is unclear, and telling direct from figurative meaning, e.g. "golden ring" and "golden hands"
evidence: Explain the meaning of a familiar word in own words
Spot a word whose meaning needs to be checked
Tell direct from figurative use
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what a word means, notice when a word is unclear and tell a direct meaning from a figurative one?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Using Dictionaries and Reference Books
topics.description: Using the alphabet to find words in dictionaries, catalogues and reference books, and choosing the right kind (spelling, explanatory, pronunciation dictionary) for a question
evidence: Put words in alphabetical order
Find a word in a dictionary quickly
Choose which dictionary answers a question
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find a word in a dictionary using alphabetical order and choose the kind of dictionary a question needs?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Languages of the World
topics.description: Language as the main means of human communication and part of culture, the many languages spoken in a country and in the world, and the roles of a native and a state language
evidence: Explain why people need language
Name several languages spoken in own country or the world
Describe where the native language is used
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what language is for and name several languages spoken in their country or the world?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: How Languages Develop and Related Languages
topics.description: Languages change over time and belong to families: new words appear, old ones go out of use, and related languages such as Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Serbian share a common origin
evidence: Give examples of words that entered or left the language
Explain that related languages come from a common source
Name several languages of the same family
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} give examples of how a language changes and name languages related to their own?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Branches of Linguistics
topics.description: Linguistics as the science of language and its main parts: phonetics, vocabulary, word structure and word formation, morphology, syntax and spelling, with the unit each one studies
evidence: Name the main branches of language study
Say which unit each branch studies (sound, word, morpheme, sentence)
Choose the branch to which a task belongs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the main branches of language study and say what each one looks at?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Observing and Investigating Language
topics.description: Studying language like a scientist: comparing examples, grouping words, forming and testing a guess, and drawing a conclusion, e.g. "Which words keep the same ending?"
evidence: Compare language examples and notice a pattern
Group words by a feature chosen by self
State a conclusion supported by examples
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} compare words or sentences, notice a pattern and explain a conclusion with examples?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Oral and Written, Monologue and Dialogue Speech
topics.description: Kinds of speech: spoken and written, one speaker (monologue) and several speakers (dialogue), and how each is formed, e.g. a story told aloud and a written note
evidence: Tell spoken from written speech
Tell a monologue from a dialogue
Compose a short monologue and a dialogue on a topic
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell a monologue from a dialogue and spoken from written speech, and make one of each?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Kinds of Listening and Reading
topics.description: Choosing how to listen or read for a purpose: selective, introductory and detailed listening; studying, introductory, skimming and searching reading
evidence: Name the kinds of listening and reading
Choose the kind that fits a task
Read a text in the chosen way to get what is needed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} choose between skimming, searching and close reading to fit what they need from a text?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Text Types: Narration, Description, Reasoning
topics.description: Three kinds of text: narration tells events in order, description shows features, reasoning gives a claim and reasons; recognising the theme and main idea of a text
evidence: Name the type of a short text
Name the theme and main idea of a text
Write a few sentences of each type
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell whether a short text narrates, describes or reasons and name its main idea?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Speech Etiquette and Respectful Dialogue
topics.description: Polite forms of speech and the rules of conversation: greeting, asking, thanking, taking turns, listening, disagreeing politely and accepting other views
evidence: Use polite forms for greeting, request and thanks
Take turns and listen in a dialogue
Disagree respectfully and give a reason
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} keep a polite conversation, wait for a turn and disagree with a reason without being rude?

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Finding and Checking Information
topics.description: Choosing a source for a task, looking things up in dictionaries and reference books, telling reliable from unreliable information and following simple safety rules online
evidence: Pick a suitable source for a question
Check a fact in a second source
Follow basic rules for safe use of the internet
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} pick a source for a question, check a fact in another source and follow safe online habits?

topics.subject: Learning to Learn
topics.name: Schemes and Tables for Findings
topics.description: Showing the result of an observation in a scheme, diagram or table, and reading information from them, e.g. a table of word groups
evidence: Read information from a scheme or table
Make a table to sort observations
Explain a diagram in words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make a simple table or scheme from what they observed and read information back from it?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Folk Sayings, Riddles and Rhymes
topics.description: Short folk forms: proverbs, idioms, similes, riddles, tongue twisters, counting rhymes and nursery rhymes, and how their meaning and sound work, e.g. "slow and steady wins the race"
evidence: Explain the meaning of a common proverb or idiom
Solve a riddle and say a tongue twister
Tell what makes a counting rhyme or nursery rhyme different from other texts
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain a familiar proverb, solve a riddle and recite a rhyme or tongue twister?

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: Literary Periods: Middle Ages to Baroque
topics.description: Reading texts from the Middle Ages, Renaissance, Reformation and Baroque and linking each to its ideas, genres and arts, e.g. chivalric culture, humanism, printing, comedy and epigram
evidence: Place a text in its period by its features
Name typical genres of the Middle Ages, Renaissance and Baroque
Compare how one work is adapted in different arts or media
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} place a text in its period and name typical genres and ideas of that period?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: True and False Statements
topics.description: Decide whether a statement about a set of things is true or false and make up simple statements of your own, such as 'all the red blocks are round'
evidence: Say whether a statement about a picture or group of objects is true or false
Make up a true and a false statement about the same group of objects
Give an example that shows why a statement is true or false
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} look at a group of objects and say whether a statement about them, like 'every block here is red', is true or false?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: All, Some and None
topics.description: Use the words all, some, not all, none, and, and not correctly to describe a group, such as 'some animals here have wings but none are fish'
evidence: Use 'all', 'some' and 'none' correctly about a group of objects
Combine two properties with 'and' and rule one out with 'not'
Fix a statement by changing a word, e.g. from 'all' to 'some'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe a group of things using words like 'all', 'some', 'none', 'and' and 'not' so the description is correct?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Sorting by Shared Properties
topics.description: Sort things into groups and name the property they share, using sorting circles and Venn-style diagrams, such as 'red and round' versus 'not red'
evidence: Sort objects into two sorting circles by a named property
Name the shared property of the items in one part of a diagram
Pick items from a set that fit a given property or combination of properties
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} sort a mixed set of objects into circles and say what property the objects in each circle have in common?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Certain, Impossible and Possible Events
topics.description: Sort events into certain, impossible and possible-but-not-certain through games and experiments, such as drawing from a bag of only red counters
evidence: Sort events into 'certain', 'impossible' and 'possible but not certain'
Guess which of two events is more likely in a simple game and test the guess by counting
Tally outcomes of a simple chance experiment and compare with the guess
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} say whether something is certain, impossible or just possible, for example what can come out of a bag holding only red counters?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Composing Word Problems
topics.description: Write a word problem for a given number sentence, picture or relationship, and use maths words to describe the story
evidence: Write a short story problem that matches a given number sentence
Change a given word problem by altering the numbers or the question
Describe a story situation using numbers, signs and maths words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} make up a short word problem that matches a given number sentence like 12 − 5 = 7?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Listing All Possible Options
topics.description: List every possible combination in a simple situation in an organised way, such as all outfits from 3 tops and 2 skirts, without missing or repeating one
evidence: List all options in a simple choice situation without repeats
Use an order or a table to make sure no option is missed
Count how many options there are and explain how the list was organised
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} list every possible outfit from 3 tops and 2 bottoms in an organised way, without missing or repeating any?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Spotting Maths in the World Around
topics.description: Notice mathematical relationships in everyday surroundings, such as part and whole, more and less, and shapes in buildings
evidence: Point out part-whole and more-less relationships in real objects or pictures
Describe an everyday situation with a maths word like 'half', 'more' or 'equal'
Find a shape or number pattern in the classroom or street
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} notice maths in everyday life, such as saying a pizza is cut into equal parts or that one pile has more than another?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Finding and Fixing Mistakes in Maths
topics.description: Check a result by another method, spot where a solution went wrong, discuss errors and correct them, such as re-adding in a different order
evidence: Check a calculation with a different method, such as the inverse operation
Find the step where a worked solution goes wrong
Explain a mistake calmly and correct it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} check a finished sum with a second method and, if the answers differ, work out where the mistake happened?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Working Together on Maths Problems
topics.description: Solve maths problems in a pair or group by agreeing on a method, sharing the work, listening to others and settling disagreements calmly
evidence: Agree with a partner on how to solve a problem and who does which part
Listen to a partner's idea and give feedback politely
Combine the group's results into one answer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} solve a maths problem with a partner, agreeing on a plan and sharing the work without arguing?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Using Digital Tools for Maths Learning
topics.description: Use electronic textbooks, calculators-style trainers and online reference safely for maths practice, and follow the steps of a digital exercise or test
evidence: Open and work through an exercise in a digital textbook or trainer
Follow the steps of an on-screen test and submit answers
Look up a maths word or fact in a trusted source with an adult's guidance
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} work through a maths exercise on a tablet or computer and look up a maths fact from a trusted source safely?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Following and Describing Step-by-Step Methods
topics.description: Use and explain step-by-step rules for calculating, measuring and drawing shapes, such as the steps of column addition or of measuring a length
evidence: Follow a written or spoken set of steps for a calculation or measurement
Explain the steps of a method in the right order
Spot a missing or misplaced step in a method
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the steps of a method they use, like column addition or measuring with a ruler, in the right order?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Graphs: Vertices and Edges
topics.description: Understand a graph as dots (vertices) joined by lines (edges), count the degree of each vertex, and see that the sum of degrees is twice the number of edges
evidence: Draw a graph for a situation such as friendships or road links
Find the degree of each vertex and check that the degrees add up to twice the number of edges
Tell whether a graph is connected and whether its edges have directions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw dots and lines to show how things are connected, such as towns and roads, and count how many lines meet at each dot?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Paths, Cycles and Euler Routes
topics.description: Follow paths and cycles in a graph, decide whether a route can cross every edge exactly once, and solve puzzles with graphs
evidence: Trace a path and a cycle in a given graph
Decide from the vertex degrees whether an Euler route exists
Solve a puzzle such as a bridge-crossing problem by drawing a graph
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} decide whether a drawing can be traced without lifting the pencil or repeating a line, by looking at how many lines meet at each point?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Lines and Planes in Space
topics.description: Describe how points, lines and planes relate in 3-D, including skew lines, a line perpendicular to a plane, and parallel and intersecting planes
evidence: Name the possible positions of two lines in space: intersecting, parallel or skew
Describe a line as parallel to, lying in, or perpendicular to a plane
Find examples of parallel and intersecting planes on a box or room
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} use a box or a room to show two lines that never meet yet are not parallel, and say what such lines are called?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Projection onto a Plane and Angle Between a Line and a Plane
topics.description: Project points, segments and lines orthogonally onto a plane, find the distance from a point to a plane, and measure the angle between a line and a plane
evidence: Draw the orthogonal projection of a segment onto a plane
Find the distance from a point to a plane as a perpendicular length
Identify the angle between a slanted line and its projection
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how the shadow of a slanted stick falling straight down onto the floor relates to the angle the stick makes with the floor?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Polyhedra
topics.description: Recognise polyhedra such as prisms and pyramids, name their faces, edges and vertices, and describe their features
evidence: Name faces, edges and vertices of a prism and a pyramid
Tell polyhedra apart from solids with curved surfaces
Count faces, edges and vertices of a given polyhedron
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} point out the faces, edges and vertices of a prism or a pyramid and say what makes a solid a polyhedron?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Pythagorean Theorem
topics.description: In a right triangle the square on the longest side equals the sum of the squares on the other two, used to find missing lengths in drawings and practical problems
evidence: State the Pythagorean theorem for a right triangle
Find a missing side of a right triangle with the theorem
Apply it to a practical problem, such as the length of a ladder against a wall
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the missing side of a right triangle, for example a ladder reaching a wall, using the Pythagorean theorem?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Central and Inscribed Angles
topics.description: Relate a central angle to an inscribed angle on the same arc, and use the fact that an inscribed angle is half the central angle in geometry problems
evidence: Identify central and inscribed angles in a circle drawing
Use that an inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc
Use that inscribed angles on the same arc are equal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find an inscribed angle in a circle when given the central angle on the same arc?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Angles Formed by Chords, Secants and Tangents
topics.description: Find angles between two chords, two secants, or a tangent and a chord from the arcs they cut off
evidence: Compute the angle between two intersecting chords from the arcs
Compute the angle between a tangent and a chord
Compute the angle between two secants meeting outside the circle
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} work out the angle between a tangent and a chord of a circle from the arc it cuts off?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Intersecting Chords and Secants Theorems
topics.description: Use the products of segments of two chords, of two secants, and the tangent-squared rule to find unknown lengths in a circle
evidence: Use the chord theorem: product of the segments is equal for two chords
Use the secant and the tangent-squared theorems
Find an unknown segment length in a circle drawing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find a missing segment of a chord in a circle, knowing the other three segments of two crossing chords?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Quadrilaterals with an Inscribed Circle
topics.description: Recognise a quadrilateral that has a circle touching all four sides, and use that opposite sides add up to equal sums to solve problems
evidence: Recognise a quadrilateral with an inscribed circle
Use that the sums of opposite sides are equal
Find an unknown side length with this property
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find an unknown side of a quadrilateral around a circle by using that opposite sides add to the same total?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Vectors
topics.description: Understand a vector as a quantity with length and direction, such as a displacement or force, and compare vectors as equal, opposite, same-direction or collinear
evidence: Draw a vector for a displacement and state its length
Tell equal, opposite and same-direction vectors apart
Recognise collinear vectors
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} draw an arrow for a movement, such as 3 steps east, and say which other arrows show the same or the opposite movement?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Vector Operations and Coordinates
topics.description: Add and subtract vectors, multiply them by a number, resolve a vector along two non-parallel vectors and write a vector in coordinates
evidence: Add and subtract two vectors by drawing and by coordinates
Multiply a vector by a number
Write a vector as a combination of two non-parallel vectors
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} add two vectors by drawing them head to tail, and by adding their coordinates?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Dot Product of Vectors
topics.description: Compute the dot product of two vectors and use it to find lengths and angles between vectors, including in geometry problems
evidence: Compute the dot product from coordinates
Use the dot product to find the angle between two vectors
Use it to find a length or check perpendicularity
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} use the dot product of two vectors to find the angle between them?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Compass and Straightedge Constructions
topics.description: Carry out basic constructions with compass and ruler, such as a perpendicular bisector, an angle bisector and a triangle from its sides
evidence: Construct a perpendicular bisector and an angle bisector
Construct a triangle from three given side lengths
Explain the steps of a construction
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} use only a compass and an unmarked ruler to find the midpoint of a segment or to bisect an angle?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Area of Polygons on Grid Paper
topics.description: Find the area of triangles and polygons drawn on squared paper by counting squares, splitting into simple shapes or enclosing in a rectangle
evidence: Find the area of a polygon on grid paper by counting squares
Split a shape into triangles and rectangles and add their areas
Enclose a shape in a rectangle and subtract the extra parts
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the area of an odd triangle drawn on squared paper by putting it inside a rectangle?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Median, Range and Spread
topics.description: Describe a data set with its mean, median, largest and smallest values and range, and say what each tells us, such as prices in several shops
evidence: Find the median and the range of a data set
Compare the mean and the median of the same data
Describe a data set from a table or chart using these measures
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} find the mean, median and range of a list of numbers, such as prices, and say what each one shows?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Random Variation and Statistical Stability
topics.description: See that measured values such as prices, heights or physical quantities vary at random, yet averages and frequencies settle down as more data is collected
evidence: Give examples of random variation in real data, such as heights or prices
Explain that repeating a measurement gives slightly different values
Observe that a relative frequency settles as the number of trials grows
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why repeated measurements of the same thing differ a little, and why the average becomes steadier with more measurements?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Modelling Real Problems with Similarity and Trigonometry
topics.description: Turn a real situation, such as the height of a tree or the slope of a ramp, into a drawing and compute lengths using similar triangles, sine, cosine and tangent
evidence: Draw a diagram for a real situation and mark known and unknown lengths
Choose between similar triangles and trigonometry to compute a length
Interpret the calculated answer in the situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} work out something like the height of a tree from its shadow by drawing a diagram and using similar triangles or trigonometry?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Branches of Biology and Careers
topics.description: The main branches of biology (botany, zoology, ecology, anatomy, cell biology) and jobs that use them, such as doctor, vet, agronomist and farmer
evidence: Name at least four branches of biology and say what each studies
Match a biology-related job to the branch it uses
Give an example of how biology connects to another science
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the main branches of biology and say what a vet or a farmer needs biology for?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Biological Terms and Sources of Information
topics.description: Using biological terms and symbols correctly and finding reliable facts in textbooks, reference books, popular-science books and the internet
evidence: Explain a new biological term in their own words
Find an answer to a biology question in two different sources
Say which of two sources is more trustworthy and why
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} look up a biology fact in a reference book or on the internet and explain the new terms they met?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Field Trips and Local Nature Study
topics.description: Studying the plants, animals and seasonal changes of the local area on a field trip or virtual tour: observing, noting and sorting what is found
evidence: Observe and record at least five local plants or animals on a trip
Describe one seasonal change seen in a natural place
Follow safety and care rules when observing living things outdoors
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} record what they find on a nature walk or virtual field trip, such as local plants, animals and signs of the season?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Natural and Artificial Communities
topics.description: Comparing natural communities (forest, pond, meadow) with artificial ones (aquarium, garden) and the living things that make them up
evidence: Name the organisms in a forest, pond or meadow community
Explain how an aquarium differs from a pond
Describe how a natural community changes with the seasons
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} compare a natural community such as a pond with an artificial one such as an aquarium?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Litter Clean-Up Action
topics.description: Planning and carrying out a litter clean-up in a nearby forest, park or the school grounds, and sorting and disposing of the waste safely
evidence: Plan a clean-up with tools, roles and safety rules
Sort collected litter into groups such as plastic, glass and paper
Explain how litter harms plants and animals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} take part in a litter clean-up and explain why litter harms nature?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Shoot, Stem and Leaf Structure
topics.description: The structure of a flowering plant's shoot: buds, stem layers and the outer and inner structure of a leaf, plus modified shoots such as rhizome, tuber and bulb
evidence: Label the parts of a shoot, a stem and a leaf
Explain how a bud develops into a shoot
Identify a rhizome, tuber and bulb and say what each stores
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} label the parts of a leaf and stem and tell a potato tuber from a bulb?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Algae, Mosses and Ferns
topics.description: Plants without seeds: green, brown and red algae, mosses, horsetails, club mosses and ferns, how they reproduce with spores and why they matter in nature
evidence: Describe how algae differ from mosses and ferns
Explain the life cycle of a fern with spores
Give a role of algae or ancient ferns in nature or for people
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe how algae, mosses and ferns differ and how ferns reproduce without seeds?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Seed Plant Groups and Families
topics.description: Comparing conifers (spruce, pine, larch) with flowering plants and recognising the traits of plant families such as crucifers, roses and legumes, including crop and weed plants
evidence: Describe the cone and needles of a conifer
Name the flower features of at least two plant families
Tell a crop plant from a weed of the local area
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell a conifer from a flowering plant and recognise a plant family from its flower?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Animal Body Organisation
topics.description: How animals support, move, feed, breathe, transport substances and are covered, and how the science of zoology links to other sciences
evidence: Compare how two animals move, feed and breathe
Name the body covering of at least three animals
Explain what zoology studies and its branches
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} compare how two different animals move, feed and breathe?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Cnidarians and Worms
topics.description: Hydra and jellyfish with their two body layers, and flat, round and segmented worms, including parasitic worms, their life cycles and earthworm structure
evidence: Describe how a hydra catches and digests food
Tell flatworms, roundworms and earthworms apart by body structure
Explain how a parasitic worm is adapted to its host
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe a hydra and compare flatworms, roundworms and earthworms?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Arthropods and Insects
topics.description: Arthropod body plan and insect structure, complete and incomplete development, the main insect orders, and insects as pests, parasites and disease carriers
evidence: Label head, thorax and abdomen of an insect
Compare complete and incomplete development with an example each
Name three insect orders with an example
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} label the body of an insect and compare how a butterfly and a grasshopper develop?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Molluscs
topics.description: Snails, bivalves and cephalopods: shells and soft bodies, habitats, feeding and reproduction, and the role of molluscs in nature and for people
evidence: Name three classes of molluscs with an example
Describe how a shell protects a mollusc
Give a use or role of molluscs in nature or for people
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the groups of molluscs and describe how a shell helps a snail or a mussel?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Chordates and Fish
topics.description: What defines chordates, from the lancelet to vertebrates, and fish in detail: body shape, gills, bony and cartilaginous fish, reproduction, migration and use
evidence: Name the features shared by all chordates
Explain how a fish's body suits life in water
Tell cartilaginous fish from bony fish
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how a fish's body suits life in water and tell a shark from a carp?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Amphibians and Reptiles
topics.description: How amphibians live in water and on land and how reptiles are adapted to dry land: skin, breathing, development, diversity and protection
evidence: Explain how a frog's life cycle links water and land
Name two adaptations of reptiles to life on land
Compare an amphibian and a reptile
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} compare a frog and a lizard and explain how each is adapted to its habitat?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Birds
topics.description: Bird body structure and adaptations for flight, feathers and skeleton, nesting and care of young, migration, ecological groups and the role of birds in nature
evidence: Name three adaptations for flight
Tell contour, down and fluff feathers apart
Explain why some birds migrate
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how a bird's body is built for flight and why some birds migrate?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Mammals
topics.description: Mammal body structure, skeleton, muscles and nervous system, care of young, egg-laying, marsupial and placental mammals, the main orders and their value or danger to people
evidence: Name three features that define mammals
Compare monotremes, marsupials and placental mammals
Match three mammal orders to examples
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name what makes an animal a mammal and sort mammals into groups such as rodents and carnivores?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: The Human as a Biosocial Species
topics.description: The sciences that study people (anatomy, physiology, psychology, hygiene), how the body is studied, and what makes humans both biological and social beings
evidence: Name three sciences that study humans and what each studies
Give examples of human biological and social traits
Explain why knowledge about the body helps keep us healthy
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name sciences that study the human body and explain how people are both biological and social beings?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Tissues and Blood Under the Microscope
topics.description: The four tissue types of the human body and the cells of blood, recognised on prepared slides and compared with frog blood
evidence: Name the four tissue types and one example of each
Tell red blood cells from white blood cells on a picture or slide
Compare human blood cells with frog blood cells
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} name the main tissue types and recognise blood cells on a microscope picture?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Skin and Excretion
topics.description: Structure of the skin, its layers, glands and role in protection and temperature, and the kidneys as organs that remove waste, with ways to prevent kidney disease
evidence: Name the layers of the skin and one function of each
Say where the kidneys are and what they filter
Give two ways to care for skin or protect kidneys
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe what skin does and where the kidneys are and what they remove from the body?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Vision and Eye Health
topics.description: Structure of the eye, how sharpness of vision is tested, common vision problems, and habits that protect eyesight
evidence: Label the main parts of the eye
Explain how a vision chart tests sharpness
Name two habits that protect eyesight
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} label the parts of the eye and explain how eyesight is tested and protected?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Memory and Attention
topics.description: Short-term and long-term memory, how mechanical and logical memorising differ, and simple tests of memory span and attention
evidence: Tell short-term from long-term memory
Run a simple memory-span test and record results
Compare learning by rote and by understanding
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain the difference between short-term and long-term memory and run a simple memory test?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Environment and Human Health
topics.description: How air, water, noise, heat and the indoor climate of homes affect health, and how to act safely in dangerous or emergency situations
evidence: Give two ways a polluted environment can harm health
Name factors of a healthy indoor climate
Describe safe behaviour in one emergency situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain how air, water and the indoor climate affect health and what to do in an emergency?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Physical Phenomena and Measuring Instruments
topics.description: Mechanical, thermal, electrical, magnetic and light phenomena, and taking direct measurements with analogue and digital instruments
evidence: Sort everyday phenomena into mechanical, thermal, electrical, magnetic and light
Read an analogue scale and a digital display
Record a direct measurement with its unit
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} sort everyday phenomena into types and read a measurement from both an analogue and a digital instrument?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Buoyancy and Archimedes' Principle
topics.description: The upward force on a body in a liquid, how it depends on the volume submerged and the liquid's density, and why objects float or sink
evidence: Measure the buoyant force with a spring balance
Show it depends on submerged volume, not on the body's mass
Design a boat or hydrometer and test how much it can carry
