topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain why a ship floats and measure the upward force on an object in water?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Intermolecular Forces and Crystal Structure
topics.description: Attraction between molecules, growing salt or sugar crystals, and how the arrangement of particles in a crystal lattice (graphite, diamond, sodium chloride) explains properties
evidence: Show with a simple experiment that molecules attract each other
Grow a salt or sugar crystal and describe it
Compare the lattices of diamond and graphite and their properties
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} grow a salt crystal and explain how the arrangement of particles gives a solid its properties?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Thermal Expansion and Gas Pressure
topics.description: Thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases, and how the pressure of a trapped gas depends on its volume and temperature
evidence: Show the expansion of a solid, liquid and gas on heating
Predict what happens to gas pressure when volume shrinks
Explain how warming or cooling changes pressure in a closed container
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} show that things expand when heated and explain how the pressure of a trapped gas changes with volume and temperature?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Uniform and Uniformly Accelerated Motion Experiments
topics.description: Building a track for a ball or cart to speed up and then move steadily, and testing that distances in equal times follow the odd-number pattern 1:3:5
evidence: Build a track and measure times and distances for a moving cart
Tell steady motion from steadily speeding-up motion in data
Check a hypothesis about distances in equal time intervals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} build a simple track, measure a cart's motion and check a prediction about how its speed changes?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Pendulum and Spring Oscillation Periods
topics.description: Measuring the period and frequency of a string pendulum and a spring pendulum and testing what the period depends on, such as mass, length and spring stiffness
evidence: Measure the period by timing many swings
Show that a string pendulum's period does not depend on mass
Find how a spring pendulum's period changes with mass and stiffness
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} measure the period of a pendulum and test which changes make it swing faster or slower?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Colour Filters and Seeing Colour
topics.description: How an object looks through red, green and blue filters, and why filters let some colours through and absorb others
evidence: Predict an object's colour through a filter
Explain that a filter absorbs part of white light
Test several objects through coloured filters and record results
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} predict how a coloured object will look through a red or green filter and explain why?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Atomic Models: Rutherford and Bohr
topics.description: How scattering experiments led to the planetary model of the atom, the Bohr model, and light emitted or absorbed in quanta
evidence: Describe what Rutherford's experiment showed about the atom
Draw the planetary model with nucleus and electrons
Explain that atoms emit or absorb light in quanta
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} describe how scientists found that an atom has a nucleus and draw a simple model of an atom?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Line and Continuous Spectra
topics.description: Observing continuous and line spectra of emission and absorption, the hydrogen spectrum and gas spectra, and how a spectrum identifies an element
evidence: Observe a continuous and a line spectrum through a spectroscope
Tell an emission spectrum from an absorption spectrum
Explain how line spectra identify elements
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell a continuous spectrum from a line spectrum and say how scientists use spectra to identify elements?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Radioactivity and Atomic Nuclei
topics.description: Alpha, beta and gamma radiation, nucleon structure of the nucleus, isotopes, half-life, nuclear reactions, and tracks in a cloud chamber or photographs
evidence: Name alpha, beta and gamma radiation and how far each penetrates
Explain half-life with a simple example
Measure background radiation or read particle tracks in a photo
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain what radioactivity and half-life mean and tell the three kinds of radiation apart?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Nuclear Energy and Radiation Effects
topics.description: Fission and fusion as energy sources of power plants, the Sun and stars, and the effect of radiation on living things and ways to limit exposure
evidence: Tell fission from fusion
Explain how a nuclear power plant makes electricity
Name ways to reduce exposure to radiation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} tell nuclear fission from fusion and explain how radiation can affect living things?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Physics in Medicine and Technology
topics.description: How physics supports medicine and modern technology: ultrasound, ECG, scanners, magnetic resonance, remote control, mobile phones and the internet
evidence: Name two physics-based medical methods and what they show
Explain how a remote control or mobile phone sends information

Suffixes come in three kinds: a képző makes a new word (ír, write → író, writer), a jel adds a meaning such as plural or past tense (-k, -t), and a rag links the word to the sentence (-ban, -t). Many suffixes have two or three forms that match the vowels of the stem: házban, kertben.

topics.subject: Language & Literature
topics.name: The Four Principles of Hungarian Spelling
topics.description: Hungarian spelling follows four principles. Pronunciation: most words are written as they sound (alma). Word analysis: a word keeps the parts it is built from even when they sound different (látja sounds like 'láttya' but is lát + ja). Tradition: some spellings keep an old form, such as ly in hely next to j in fej, and old family names like Kossuth or Széchenyi. Simplification: where a suffix would give three identical letters, only two are written (toll + val → tollal).

Old Hungarians also wrote in a runic script (rovásírás), carved into wood. Over the centuries Hungarian took loanwords from Turkic, Slavic, Latin and German, and in the language reform around 1800 Kazinczy and other writers created thousands of new words.
